title: knowledge/ scaffolding: directory, requirements.txt, pom.xml, curated_baseline.md stub
content:
Create the `knowledge/` directory and its static files. Nothing in this issue runs code — it just establishes the skeleton that the other issues build on.

## Files to create

### `knowledge/requirements.txt`
Pin all Python dependencies needed by `build.py`:
- `sentence-transformers` (for bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings)
- `rank-bm25` (for BM25 index)
- `python-frontmatter` (for parsing YAML frontmatter in markdown)
- Any transitive pinning needed for reproducibility (use `pip-compile` or equivalent)

Maven coordinates:
```xml
<groupId>com.manetu</groupId>
<artifactId>mpe-knowledge</artifactId>
<version>${project.version}</version>
<packaging>jar</packaging>
```
Version is injected at build time via `-Dproject.version=...`. Include `distributionManagement` pointing to GitHub Packages (`https://maven.pkg.github.com/manetu/policyengine`).

### `knowledge/curated_baseline.md`
Initial hand-curated MPE essentials stub (~1–2 K tokens). Plain UTF-8 Markdown, no frontmatter, safe to prepend verbatim to an LLM system prompt. Cover at minimum:
- What PolicyEngine is and what problem it solves
- Core PORC model (Principals, Operations, Resources, Conditions)
- PolicyDomain YAML structure overview
- Key CLI commands (`mpe lint`, `mpe test`, `mpe serve`)

This file will evolve — the initial version just needs to be a useful skeleton that a developer can refine.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `knowledge/requirements.txt` exists with pinned versions for all needed deps
- [ ] `knowledge/pom.xml` is valid Maven POM with correct coordinates; version is a placeholder/property, not hardcoded
- [ ] `knowledge/curated_baseline.md` contains meaningful content (~500–2000 tokens), no frontmatter, renders as valid Markdown
- [ ] No code files yet (build.py, Makefile) — those are in subsequent issues

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): IMPLEMENTED, with intentional spec divergence (commits de42350/5a48cc9). `knowledge/` exists with all four files tracked: `requirements.txt`, `pom.xml`, `curated_baseline.md` (321 lines, well beyond a stub, covers PolicyEngine/PORC/PolicyDomain YAML/CLI), plus `build.py`/`Makefile` from the later issues in this same batch. **Divergence #1 (publishing):** `pom.xml` uses `groupId io.github.manetu` (not `com.manetu`) with no GitHub-Packages `distributionManagement` — the pipeline publishes to Clojars instead (see [[i-4uan]]/[[i-1ezw]]). **Divergence #2 (embeddings):** `requirements.txt` has no `sentence-transformers` — embeddings are generated via an Ollama HTTP call instead (see [[i-3ca4]]). Both divergences are deliberate per the commit messages, not omissions. Closing; spec [[s-1ka5]] is being updated separately to stop describing the superseded GitHub-Packages/com.manetu/bge-small-en-v1.5 design as current.

title: build.py: document chunker — walk docs/docs/ and split at H2 + code-fence boundaries
content:
Implement the document chunking phase of `knowledge/build.py`. This is the first pipeline stage; its output feeds the embedding and BM25 stages.

## Behavior

Walk all `.md` files under `docs/docs/` (recursively). For each file:

1. Parse YAML frontmatter (if present) via `python-frontmatter`.
2. Split the body at **H2 (`##`) heading boundaries**. Each H2 section becomes one or more chunks.
3. Within an H2 section, if the section exceeds a configurable token budget (default: ~500 tokens estimated by word count), further split at **code-fence boundaries** (``` ``` ```). Prefer not to break mid-fence.
4. For each chunk, emit:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "<stable-hash>",
     "path": "docs/docs/concepts/pbac.md",
     "heading_path": ["PBAC", "How It Works"],
     "frontmatter": { ... },
     "text": "..."
   }
   ```
   - `id`: SHA-256 of `path + heading_path + text` (first 16 hex chars is fine), stable for the same doc commit
   - `heading_path`: ordered array of headings from H1 down to the current H2 (include H1 title if present as first element)
   - `text`: the raw Markdown text of the chunk, including the heading line itself

## Output
Write all chunks (one JSON object per line) to `knowledge/target/chunks.jsonl`. Log chunk count to stdout.

## Module structure
`build.py` should be organized so the chunker is a clearly delimited function/module that can be called independently and tested. The top-level `main()` calls stages in order.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `knowledge/build.py` exists with a `chunk_documents(docs_root) -> list[dict]` function
- [ ] Running `python knowledge/build.py --stage=chunk` against the real `docs/docs/` tree produces a valid `knowledge/target/chunks.jsonl`
- [ ] Every line in `chunks.jsonl` is valid JSON with all required fields (`id`, `path`, `heading_path`, `frontmatter`, `text`)
- [ ] The same docs commit produces identical `chunks.jsonl` output on repeated runs (deterministic)
- [ ] Chunk count logged to stdout

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED, matches spec cleanly, no divergence. `knowledge/build.py:132` `chunk_documents(docs_root)` walks `docs/docs/` via sorted `rglob("*.md")` (deterministic ordering), loads frontmatter, splits at H2 boundaries (`:166-179`) and further at code-fence boundaries when a section exceeds the token budget (`_split_at_code_fences`, `:73`, triggered `:197-200`). Emits `{id, path, heading_path, frontmatter, text}` per chunk (`:206-213`) with a stable `sha256(path|heading_path|text)[:16]` id. `--stage=chunk` writes `target/chunks.jsonl`. No longer blocked — its dependency [[i-3u0x]] is satisfied. Closing.

title: build.py: embedding pipeline — generate vectors.bin using bge-small-en-v1.5
content:
Implement the embedding stage of `knowledge/build.py`. Reads chunks produced by the chunker and emits a packed float32 binary.

## Behavior

1. Load the `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model via `sentence-transformers` (downloads and caches to `~/.cache/huggingface/` on first run).
2. Encode `chunk["text"]` for each chunk in `chunks.jsonl` order, producing a 384-dimensional float32 vector per chunk.
3. Write all vectors row-major to `knowledge/target/vectors.bin` as raw `float32` (little-endian). Row `i` corresponds to chunk `i` in `chunks.jsonl` order. Total bytes = `chunk_count × 384 × 4`.

## Performance
- Use batched encoding (batch size 32 or configurable) for CPU efficiency.
- Log estimated time and throughput (chunks/sec) to stdout.

## Determinism
For the same input `chunks.jsonl` and same model version, the output `vectors.bin` must be byte-identical across runs (no random seeds, no float non-determinism from parallelism). Pin model revision if needed.

## `manifest.json` fields contributed by this stage
```json
{
  "embed_model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5",
  "embed_dims": 384
}
```

## Module structure
`embed_chunks(chunks: list[dict]) -> np.ndarray` function in `build.py`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `embed_chunks()` function exists in `build.py`
- [ ] Running `python knowledge/build.py --stage=embed` produces `knowledge/target/vectors.bin`
- [ ] File size = `chunk_count × 384 × 4` bytes (validated in script with assertion)
- [ ] Row `i` is the float32 embedding of chunk `i` from `chunks.jsonl`
- [ ] Two runs on same input produce byte-identical `vectors.bin`
- [ ] `embed_model` and `embed_dims` values are accessible for `manifest.json` assembly

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): IMPLEMENTED (functional), with intentional model/dims divergence from the spec text (though the spec's own `manifest.json` example already specified 768d + `search_query:` prefix — inconsistent with its stated "bge-small-en-v1.5, 384d" prose). `knowledge/build.py:223` `embed_chunks` calls Ollama's `nomic-embed-text:v1.5` (768d) over HTTP, batched (`EMBED_BATCH_SIZE=4`, configurable), with 3x retry on 5xx. `run_embed` (`:324-330`) writes `vectors.bin` as little-endian float32, size-asserted against `chunk_count × EMBED_DIMS × 4`. `--stage=embed` supported. **Caveat carried forward, not fixed:** determinism is weaker than the spec's "byte-identical output for the same doc commit" goal, since it depends on a live Ollama service rather than a pinned local model — acceptable given the deliberate Ollama pivot, but worth knowing if strict build reproducibility is later required. Closing; no longer blocked (dependency [[i-wqc4]] satisfied).

title: build.py: BM25 lexical index — build, serialize, and document binary format
content:
Implement the BM25 index stage of `knowledge/build.py` and document the binary serialization format in the spec's Consumer Contract section.

## Behavior

1. Build a BM25 index over all chunk texts using `rank-bm25` (`BM25Okapi` with `k1=1.2, b=0.75`).
2. Serialize the index to `knowledge/target/lexical-index.bin` in a documented binary format (see below).
3. After implementation, update `specs/s-1ka5_knowledge_artifact.md` to fill in the "BM25 serialization format" placeholder with the actual binary layout.

## Binary serialization format (to implement + document)

Design a simple, language-agnostic binary format. Suggested layout:

```
Header (16 bytes):
  magic:    4 bytes  "BM25"
  version:  2 bytes  uint16 LE, value=1
  k1:       4 bytes  float32 LE
  b:        4 bytes  float32 LE
  reserved: 2 bytes  zeros

Vocabulary section:
  vocab_size: 4 bytes uint32 LE
  For each term (vocab_size entries):
    term_len:  2 bytes uint16 LE
    term:      term_len bytes UTF-8
    idf:       4 bytes float32 LE

Postings section:
  For each term (same order as vocabulary):
    posting_count: 4 bytes uint32 LE
    For each posting:
      chunk_id:  4 bytes uint32 LE  (index into chunks.jsonl)
      tf_score:  4 bytes float32 LE
```

The exact format is flexible — document whatever you implement. The key constraint is that a Clojure consumer can deserialize it without calling Python.

## Spec update
After implementing, update `specs/s-1ka5_knowledge_artifact.md` section "BM25 serialization format" with the actual binary layout (byte offsets, types, endianness).

## Module structure
`build_lexical_index(chunks: list[dict]) -> bytes` function in `build.py`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `build_lexical_index()` exists in `build.py` and writes `knowledge/target/lexical-index.bin`
- [ ] Binary file starts with magic bytes `BM25` (for basic validation by consumers)
- [ ] `specs/s-1ka5_knowledge_artifact.md` "BM25 serialization format" section filled in with actual byte layout
- [ ] A small round-trip test: serialize → deserialize in Python, confirm a known term's IDF and posting list are recoverable
- [ ] Two runs on same input produce byte-identical `lexical-index.bin`

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED, matches spec byte-for-byte, no divergence. `knowledge/build.py:343-422` `build_lexical_index` — magic `b"BM25"`, uint16 version=1, float32 k1=1.2/b=0.75, 2-byte reserved (`:402-406`); vocab section (`vocab_size` uint32 + per-term `term_len` uint16/UTF-8 bytes/`idf` float32, `:409-414`); postings section (`posting_count` uint32 + `chunk_id` uint32/`tf_score` float32, `:417-422`) — all little-endian, vocab sorted alphabetically, postings sorted by ascending chunk_id, exactly per spec's BM25 Serialization Format section (which is itself already filled in on [[s-1ka5]]). A round-trip deserializer + self-test (`_deserialize_lexical_index`/`_test_lexical_round_trip`, `:427,489`) is invoked from `run_lexical`. Approving from needs_review → closed.

title: build.py: artifact assembly — pack JAR, emit manifest.json, log sha256 fingerprint
content:
Implement the final assembly stage of `knowledge/build.py` that combines all intermediate outputs into the distributable JAR.

## Behavior

1. Read `chunks.jsonl`, `vectors.bin`, `lexical-index.bin` from `knowledge/target/`.
2. Read `curated_baseline.md` from `knowledge/`.
3. Build `manifest.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "manifest_version": 1,
     "mpe_version": "<from git describe>",
     "embed_model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5",
     "embed_dims": 384,
     "chunk_count": <line count of chunks.jsonl>,
     "build_timestamp": "<ISO-8601 UTC>",
     "doc_commit_sha": "<git rev-parse HEAD>"
   }
   ```
4. Validate consistency: assert `chunk_count` == line count of `chunks.jsonl` == row count implied by `vectors.bin` size.
5. Assemble a ZIP (`.jar`) at `knowledge/target/mpe-knowledge-<version>.jar`:
   ```
   manifest.json
   curated_baseline.md
   chunks.jsonl
   vectors.bin
   lexical-index.bin
   META-INF/maven/com.manetu/mpe-knowledge/pom.xml
   ```
6. Log a sha256 fingerprint of the jar contents to stdout (excluding `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` timestamp bytes if Java adds one). Format: `sha256: <hex>  mpe-knowledge-<version>.jar`

## Version sourcing
Use `git describe --tags --always --dirty`. If not in a git repo, fallback to `dev`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Running `python knowledge/build.py` (no flags) runs all stages end-to-end and produces `knowledge/target/mpe-knowledge-<version>.jar`
- [ ] JAR contains exactly: `manifest.json`, `curated_baseline.md`, `chunks.jsonl`, `vectors.bin`, `lexical-index.bin`, `META-INF/maven/com.manetu/mpe-knowledge/pom.xml`
- [ ] `manifest.json` parses and all required fields are present with correct types
- [ ] `manifest_version` is `1`
- [ ] `chunk_count` matches `chunks.jsonl` line count
- [ ] `embed_dims × chunk_count × 4` == `vectors.bin` file size (validated by script)
- [ ] sha256 fingerprint logged to stdout on every run
- [ ] Two runs on the same git commit (same docs state) produce matching sha256 fingerprints (modulo `build_timestamp`)

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): IMPLEMENTED, with the same Clojars/embed-dims divergence as siblings. `knowledge/build.py:525` `run_assemble` validates prerequisite files and `vectors.bin`'s size against `chunk_count × EMBED_DIMS × 4` (`:546-554`); builds `manifest.json` (`:582-592`) with `manifest_version:1` plus a superset of the spec's required fields (also `embed_model_digest`, `embed_query_prefix`); packs the JAR with all required entries including `META-INF/maven/io.github.manetu/mpe-knowledge/pom.xml` (`:598-604`, path reflects the Clojars groupId — see [[i-3u0x]]); logs a sha256 fingerprint over sorted zip-entry contents excluding timestamp bytes (`:606-614`), matching the spec's determinism requirement. Version resolution via `MPE_VERSION` env or `git describe --tags --always --dirty` (`:556-568`). Closing; no longer blocked.

title: Makefile: knowledge-build, knowledge-install, knowledge-deploy targets
content:
Add `knowledge/Makefile` and wire its targets into the root `Makefile`.

## `knowledge/Makefile`

```makefile
VENV := knowledge/.venv
PYTHON := $(VENV)/bin/python
PIP := $(VENV)/bin/pip
VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo "dev")
TARGET := knowledge/target/mpe-knowledge-$(VERSION).jar

.PHONY: knowledge-build knowledge-install knowledge-deploy knowledge-clean

$(VENV): knowledge/requirements.txt
	python3 -m venv $(VENV)
	$(PIP) install --upgrade pip
	$(PIP) install -r knowledge/requirements.txt

knowledge-build: $(VENV)  ## Build the knowledge JAR
	mkdir -p knowledge/target
	$(PYTHON) knowledge/build.py

knowledge-install: knowledge-build  ## Install JAR to ~/.m2 (for local iamlite dev)
	mvn install:install-file \
	  -Dfile=$(TARGET) \
	  -DgroupId=com.manetu \
	  -DartifactId=mpe-knowledge \
	  -Dversion=$(VERSION) \
	  -Dpackaging=jar

knowledge-deploy: knowledge-build  ## Deploy JAR to GitHub Packages (CI only)
	mvn deploy:deploy-file \
	  -Dfile=$(TARGET) \
	  -DgroupId=com.manetu \
	  -DartifactId=mpe-knowledge \
	  -Dversion=$(VERSION) \
	  -Dpackaging=jar \
	  -DrepositoryId=github \
	  -Durl=https://maven.pkg.github.com/manetu/policyengine

knowledge-clean:
	rm -rf knowledge/target
```

## Root `Makefile` additions
Add the following targets (delegating to `knowledge/Makefile`):
```makefile
knowledge-build: ## Build the knowledge artifact JAR
	@$(MAKE) -f knowledge/Makefile knowledge-build

knowledge-install: ## Install knowledge JAR to ~/.m2
	@$(MAKE) -f knowledge/Makefile knowledge-install

knowledge-deploy: ## Deploy knowledge JAR to GitHub Packages (CI)
	@$(MAKE) -f knowledge/Makefile knowledge-deploy
```

Also extend the `clean` target to call `knowledge-clean`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `make knowledge-build` from repo root creates `knowledge/target/mpe-knowledge-<version>.jar`
- [ ] On first run, a Python venv is created under `knowledge/.venv` and deps installed from `requirements.txt`
- [ ] On subsequent runs, venv creation is skipped (Make dependency on `requirements.txt`)
- [ ] `make knowledge-install` runs `mvn install:install-file` and the jar is findable at `~/.m2/repository/com/manetu/mpe-knowledge/`
- [ ] `make knowledge-deploy` runs `mvn deploy:deploy-file` targeting GitHub Packages (does not require auth locally — auth is provided by CI environment)
- [ ] `make clean` removes `knowledge/target/`
- [ ] `make help` lists the three new targets with descriptions

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): IMPLEMENTED, with the deliberate Clojars pivot from commit 5a48cc9. `knowledge/Makefile` has all three targets: `knowledge-build` (venv setup gated on `requirements.txt` mtime, runs `build.py`, plus Ollama reachability/model-pull checks), `knowledge-install` (`mvn install:install-file` to `~/.m2`), `knowledge-deploy` (`mvn deploy:deploy-file` to **Clojars** — `repositoryId=clojars`, `url=https://repo.clojars.org/` — not GitHub Packages as originally specced). Root `Makefile` delegates via `knowledge-*` targets with `.PHONY` and `## `-style help text, and `clean` cascades to `knowledge-clean`. **One minor stale artifact left behind by the pivot, noted for whoever next touches this file rather than filing separately:** root `Makefile:86`'s help string still reads "Deploy knowledge JAR to GitHub Packages (CI)" though the target now deploys to Clojars — purely cosmetic, doesn't affect behavior. Closing.

title: GH Actions: publish-knowledge.yml — build and publish knowledge artifact on release
content:
Add `.github/workflows/publish-knowledge.yml` that triggers on release tags, builds the knowledge artifact, publishes to GitHub Packages, and attaches it to the GitHub Release.

## Workflow design

Trigger: `on: release: types: [created]` (same pattern as `release-go.yml`).

Permissions:
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: write      # attach release asset
  packages: write      # push to GitHub Packages
```

### Steps

1. `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0` (needed for `git describe`)
2. `actions/setup-python@v5` with Python 3.11; cache `pip` keyed on `knowledge/requirements.txt`
3. `make knowledge-build` — produces `knowledge/target/mpe-knowledge-<VERSION>.jar`
4. `actions/setup-java@v4` with Java 17 (Temurin); configure `settings.xml` for GitHub Packages auth using `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`
5. `make knowledge-deploy` — `mvn deploy` to `https://maven.pkg.github.com/manetu/policyengine`
6. `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` — attach the jar as a release asset

### Maven settings.xml
The workflow must write a `~/.m2/settings.xml` that injects GitHub Packages credentials:
```xml
<server>
  <id>github</id>
  <username>${env.GITHUB_ACTOR}</username>
  <password>${env.GITHUB_TOKEN}</password>
</server>
```

### Version passing
Extract version from the release tag:
```bash
VERSION=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
```
Pass as `VERSION=$VERSION make knowledge-build` so the jar filename is deterministic.

### Cache
Cache the Hugging Face model cache (`~/.cache/huggingface/`) keyed on `knowledge/requirements.txt` hash to avoid re-downloading the ~33 MB model on every release.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Workflow file exists at `.github/workflows/publish-knowledge.yml`
- [ ] Triggers only on `release: types: [created]` (not on push/PR)
- [ ] Uses pinned action SHAs (matching the pattern in other workflows in this repo)
- [ ] `knowledge-build` step produces the JAR with version matching the release tag
- [ ] `knowledge-deploy` step pushes to GitHub Packages without manual token configuration
- [ ] JAR is attached as a release asset on the GitHub Release page
- [ ] Hugging Face model is cached between runs
- [ ] Workflow can be re-run without failure if JAR already exists in release assets (idempotent)

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): IMPLEMENTED, with the deliberate Clojars/Ollama pivot from commit 5a48cc9. `.github/workflows/publish-knowledge.yml` exists: triggers on `release: types: [created]`; SHA-pinned checkout/setup-python/pip-cache steps; version extraction strips `refs/tags/` and a leading `v`; runs `make knowledge-build` with Ollama env vars; idempotently checks Clojars before `make knowledge-deploy` (skips re-deploy if the version already exists); attaches the JAR via `softprops/action-gh-release`. **Divergences, all consistent with the pivot, not omissions:** workflow permissions are `contents: write` only (no `packages: write`, since it no longer publishes to GH Packages); Maven `settings.xml` carries Clojars credentials (`CLOJARS_USERNAME`/`CLOJARS_PASSWORD`) instead of a GitHub token; caches `~/.ollama/models` instead of a HuggingFace cache, with added Ollama install/start/pull-model steps. **One real minor gap carried forward:** `actions/setup-java@v4` is not SHA-pinned (comment "pin SHA when available"), unlike every other step in this workflow — worth a follow-up if SHA-pinning all actions is a hard CI requirement, but not blocking closure of this issue's core scope. Closing.

title: Fix --require-anchor bypass for multi-record (set) bundles
content:
## Problem

`verifyMultiRecord`'s immudb/rekor aggregation loops iterate the **bundle-supplied** `anchor_refs_by_root` map directly, instead of the authoritative root list (`signed_roots`). If that map is entirely absent, empty, or a given root's entry is a non-map value (`null`, a string, etc.), the loop body never executes for that root:

```go
// pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:541-567 (immudb) and 569-595 (rekor) — same pattern in both
for _, v := range anchorRefsByRoot {
    m, ok := v.(map[string]interface{})
    if !ok {
        continue   // silently skips this root's anchor requirement entirely
    }
    r := VerifyImmudbAnchor(m, opts.ImmudbPublicKey, opts.RequireAnchor.Immudb)
    if r.Status == AnchorFailed {
        immudbAnyFail = true
    }
}
```

When the outer map is absent/empty, `immudbAnyFail`/`rekorAnyFail` stay `false` and `Result.ImmudbResult`/`RekorResult` stay `nil`. Downstream in `VerifyBundle`:

```go
immudbFail := result.ImmudbResult != nil && result.ImmudbResult.Status == AnchorFailed
```

A `nil` result is treated as "not failed" — so **`--require-anchor immudb`/`rekor` can be fully defeated for an entire set bundle** just by stripping/omitting `anchor_refs_by_root`, or defeated for a single root by making that root's entry non-map.

This is asymmetric with `verifySingleRecord`, which always calls `VerifyImmudbAnchor`/`VerifyRekorAnchor` exactly once (even with a `nil` `anchor_refs`), so the single-record path correctly fails closed.

## Verified

Hand-traced by two independent review agents plus the reviewing session itself (read the code directly and confirmed the control flow). `TestVerifyBundleSetRequiredAnchorAbsentFails` only covers per-root *empty inner maps* (outer key present, inner map `{}`) — it does not cover the outer map being absent or a root's entry being non-map, so this gap is untested.

## Failure scenario

Take a legitimately-signed multi-record bundle, delete `anchor_refs_by_root` entirely (or replace one root's entry with `null`), call `VerifyBundle(bundle, pubKey, now, Options{RequireAnchor: RequireAnchor{Immudb: true, Rekor: true}})`. Result: `SetStatus=SetComplete`, `ExitCode=0` — a "fully verified" result with zero anchor verification performed for the affected root(s), despite the operator explicitly requiring it.

## Suggested fix

Iterate over the authoritative root list derived from `signed_roots` (not `anchor_refs_by_root`'s own keys), and for each known root ID do a nil-safe lookup `anchorRefsByRoot[rootID]` before calling `VerifyImmudbAnchor`/`VerifyRekorAnchor` — exactly once per known root, mirroring `verifySingleRecord`'s "always call, even with nil" pattern. A non-map value for a given root's entry should be treated the same as "absent" (pass an empty/nil map through) rather than skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-root anchor checks are driven by `signed_roots`' key set, not `anchor_refs_by_root`'s own keys.
- [ ] A missing `anchor_refs_by_root` map, and a non-map per-root entry, both correctly produce `AnchorFailed`/`ExitCode != 0` when `RequireAnchor` is set.
- [ ] Regression test: multi-record bundle with `anchor_refs_by_root` deleted entirely + `RequireAnchor.Immudb=true` → assert `ExitCode != 0`.
- [ ] Regression test: multi-record bundle with one root's `anchor_refs_by_root[id]` set to `null` + `RequireAnchor.Rekor=true` → assert `ExitCode != 0`.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:541-595`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`

title: Fix Rekor Merkle inclusion-proof promoted-node decoding bug
content:
## Problem

`rekorAuditPath` derives each proof step's sibling side from raw `logIndex` parity, halving `idx` once per **emitted hash**:

```go
// pkg/audit/verify/rekor.go:85-101
func rekorAuditPath(hashes []string, logIndex int64) ([]ProofStep, error) {
    steps := make([]ProofStep, 0, len(hashes))
    idx := logIndex
    for _, hx := range hashes {
        ...
        side := SideRight
        if idx%2 != 0 {
            side = SideLeft
        }
        steps = append(steps, ProofStep{Hash: h, Side: side})
        idx /= 2
    }
    return steps, nil
}
```

RFC 6962's odd-count "promoted node" rule (already correctly implemented in this same package's `merkle.go` `InclusionProof`/`nextLevel`) means some tree levels emit **no** proof-hash entry at all — the last node in an odd-count level is promoted upward unchanged. Real Rekor/Trillian inclusion proofs (used for any non-power-of-two tree, i.e. almost every real query) skip those levels. `idx` must be halved at **every** tree level, whether or not that level emitted a hash — but `rekorAuditPath` only halves once per hash actually present in the `hashes` array, so any promoted level along the path desyncs `idx` from the true tree-level index for every subsequent (higher) level, producing a wrong `Side` for that and all following proof steps.

## Verified

Hand-traced against this package's own `merkle.go`: for a 3-leaf tree with leaves `h0,h1,h2` and `leafIndex=2` (a promoted-node case: `level0=[h0,h1,h2]` promotes `h2` unchanged into `level1=[node(h0,h1), h2]`), `InclusionProof` correctly produces a single proof step `{Hash: node(h0,h1), Side: Left}`. Feeding the equivalent `hashes=[hex(node(h0,h1))], logIndex=2` into `rekorAuditPath` computes `Side: Right` instead — the sibling-order is inverted, which produces the wrong root hash and causes `VerifyRekorInclusion` to reject a **genuinely valid** proof.

This fails *closed* (false rejection, not a forgery — no security bypass), but breaks real-world usability: current `rekor_test.go` fixtures `(logIndex, treeSize)` = `(2,5)`, `(1,4)`, `(0,3)` all happen to avoid a promoted-node path for the chosen leaf, so the bug is fully masked by the existing test suite.

## Suggested fix

Pass `treeSize` into `VerifyRekorInclusion`/`rekorAuditPath` and port the standard `fn`/`sn` (node/last-node) recursive-halving decode used by Trillian/`certificate-transparency-go`'s `merkle/logverifier.go` `RootFromInclusionProof`, or equivalently reuse the promotion-aware logic already present in `merkle.go`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rekorAuditPath`/`VerifyRekorInclusion` correctly decode inclusion proofs for non-power-of-two tree sizes, including a leaf whose path crosses a promoted node.
- [ ] Add a test built from genuine `BuildTree`/`InclusionProof` output at `logIndex == treeSize-1` for an odd `treeSize` (guaranteed promoted-node path) — this test should fail against the current code and pass after the fix.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor.go:85-119`
- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor_test.go`
- `pkg/audit/verify/merkle.go` (reference implementation of correct promotion handling)

title: Fix nondeterministic root ordering in verifyMultiRecord when covered_range is missing
content:
## Problem

```go
// pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:452-474
roots := make([]rootEntry, 0, len(signedRoots))
for id, v := range signedRoots {          // Go map iteration -- randomized per run
    ...
}
...
sortedRoots := roots
if allHaveCoveredRange {
    sort.SliceStable(sortedRoots, ...)     // only sorted in THIS branch
}
```

`roots` is built by iterating `signedRoots`, a `map[string]interface{}`. Go map iteration order is intentionally randomized per process. When every root carries `covered_range`, this is masked by the subsequent `sort.SliceStable` by `from_seq`. But when **any** root lacks `covered_range` (`allHaveCoveredRange == false`), `sortedRoots` is left in random order, and that random order then drives: the chain-link walk (`innerOK`/`gapAt` → `chainStatus` → `derivedContiguous`), `rangeContiguous`, `spanOK` (via `sortedRoots[0]`/`sortedRoots[len-1]`), `floorOK` (retention floor uses `sortedRoots[0]`), and `outerCaveat` (genesis check uses `sortedRoots[0]`).

## Verified

Confirmed by reading the code directly — this is genuine Go map-iteration-order behavior, not a hypothetical. An offline, "same bytes -> same verdict" verifier must never depend on it.

## Failure scenario

A legitimate multi-root bundle containing one root without `covered_range` (e.g. a heartbeat/idle-partition root that by design never carries one) is submitted to the verifier twice with identical bytes. It can report `ExitCode 0` on one run and `ExitCode 1` on another, purely due to map iteration order — an unacceptable property for an audit tool whose entire purpose is a reproducible verdict.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) make the base order of `roots` deterministic unconditionally — e.g. stable-sort by `id` first, then re-sort by `from_seq` only when `allHaveCoveredRange` — or (b) since completeness derivation fundamentally depends on `covered_range`, treat "any root missing `covered_range`" as a hard `derivedContiguous = false` (fail closed) rather than falling back to an unordered walk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `verifyMultiRecord`'s root ordering is deterministic regardless of `covered_range` presence, for any input bundle bytes.
- [ ] Add a test constructing a multi-root bundle where a root is entirely missing `covered_range` and asserting a stable, deterministic result across repeated calls (e.g. run `VerifyBundle` N times on the same bundle and assert identical `ExitCode`/`ChainOK`).

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:452-474`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`

title: Document prev_signed_root field; remove/clarify stale root_chain_context in bundle-schema doc
content:
## Problem

`docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md` (lines ~59-130, 341) documents a top-level field `root_chain_context: {prev_root_id, prev_root_hash_b64}` and a Security Notes bullet describing it as the chain-linking mechanism. Grepping `pkg/audit/verify` confirms `root_chain_context` is **never read anywhere**. The real Step-5 chain check (`VerifyRootChain`, `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:186-211`) instead reads a completely different, undocumented top-level bundle key, `prev_signed_root` (`verify.go:321`), which must hold the **entire predecessor `signed_root` map** (not just two scalar fields), so the verifier can re-verify the predecessor's own signature (`VerifyRootSignature(prevSignedRoot, pubKey)`) and hash-link it.

## Failure scenario

Anyone implementing a bundle producer or independent verifier from this doc will never emit/expect `prev_signed_root`. Every non-genesis single-record bundle silently falls into `ChainCaveat` ("predecessor not embedded; full walk is the in-service job") forever, instead of ever reaching a real `ChainOK`/`ChainFailed` result — with no hint in the doc that this is happening or why, since the field it describes (`root_chain_context`) does nothing.

## Suggested fix

Add `prev_signed_root` (full predecessor `signed_root` object) to the JSON schema and Field Reference. Remove `root_chain_context` from the doc, or clearly mark it as legacy/unused-by-verifier metadata if it's genuinely present in real bundles for other reasons.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema doc's chain-linking section matches `verify.go`'s actual `prev_signed_root` field, including an example.
- [ ] `root_chain_context` either removed from the doc or explicitly marked as not consumed by the verifier.

title: Implement (or accurately un-claim) the tree_size interior-gap density check for set bundles
content:
## Problem

`docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md` Step 7.4 states, in normative language, that "check 4 must be performed independently" for `tree_size == to_seq - from_seq + 1`, and its Field Reference calls `signed_root.tree_size` the **"Authoritative interior-gap indicator."** This implies `mpe verify` performs this check. It does not: `derivedContiguous` in `verifyMultiRecord` is only `chainContiguousPass && rangeContiguous && spanOK` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`) — none of these touch `tree_size` vs. the span width, and `verify_test.go` has no fixture exercising a sparse/interior-gap batch.

## Failure scenario

A malicious or buggy batch with an interior id-dedup drop (dense `covered_range` endpoints, but `tree_size` less than the span) passes `mpe verify` with `ExitCode 0`/`SetComplete`, even though the doc explicitly tells an auditor this exact tamper class is detectable and checked. This is precisely the scenario the doc cites as the reason the check exists.

## Suggested fix

Either:
(a) Implement the per-root density check in `verifyMultiRecord`: for each root in `signed_roots`, compare `tree_size` against `covered_range.to_seq - covered_range.from_seq + 1`, fold the result into `derivedContiguous`, and add a regression test with a sparse/interior-gap fixture; or
(b) If implementing this is out of scope for now, soften the doc's normative claim and clearly flag it as a manual/out-of-band check the tool does not currently automate.

Preference: (a), since this is exactly the "cryptographic evidence over self-asserted completeness" guarantee the package's own doc.go promises for set bundles.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Either the density check is implemented and covered by a regression test, or the doc is corrected to not claim it's automated.
- [ ] If implemented: a set bundle with dense `covered_range` endpoints but an inconsistent (too-small) `tree_size` on any root is detected as incomplete/tampered.

title: Surface FloorOK==nil (unparseable retention_policy) in CLI printResult output
content:
## Problem

`VerifyBundle` sets `ExitCode = 1` when `result.FloorOK == nil` (unparseable `retention_policy`, e.g. unknown `mode` — see `pkg/audit/verify/retention.go:93-116`'s explicit "fail-closed, callers must treat nil as a failure, never as a silent pass" contract). But `printResult` only has a branch for `!*FloorOK` (false); there is no `else if result.FloorOK == nil` branch:

```go
// cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:98-100
if result.FloorOK != nil && !*result.FloorOK {
    fmt.Fprintln(w, "Retention floor: WARNING — record seq below authorized floor")
}
```

## Failure scenario

An operator (or a script grepping for `TAMPERED`/`FAILED`) sees `ExitCode 1` alongside a report that looks entirely clean — `VERIFIED`, `Root signature: OK`, `Chain continuity: OK`, no anchor failures — with zero indication of *why* verification failed. For a compliance/audit tool this reads as a bug in the tool itself. Untested: no fixture exercises this branch.

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit branch, e.g.:
```go
} else if result.FloorOK == nil {
    fmt.Fprintln(w, "Retention floor: ERROR — could not parse retention_policy")
}
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `printResult` prints a distinct, actionable line when `FloorOK == nil`.
- [ ] Add a test case constructing a bundle with an unknown `retention_policy.mode`, running it through `Run()`, and asserting the printed output explains the failure and `ExitCode == 1`.
- [ ] Also update `docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md`'s exit-code table to mention this cause (see linked docs issue for the broader exit-code table gap).

title: Restrict ParsePublicKey's ECDSA acceptance to P-256 only
content:
## Problem

```go
// pkg/audit/verify/keys.go:31-36
switch pub.(type) {
case ed25519.PublicKey, *ecdsa.PublicKey:
    return pub, nil
default:
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("verify: unsupported public key type %T", pub)
}
```

This accepts **any** ECDSA curve, not just P-256, despite `doc.go`/`keys.go`'s own documentation stating Ed25519/ECDSA-P256 are the only two supported algorithms (also stated in `docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md`'s "Cryptographic Algorithms" section). There is no `k.Curve == elliptic.P256()` check.

## Impact

Not attacker-exploitable via bundle content — the public key is out-of-band, operator-trusted input, never selected by the bundle itself — but it's a real gap relative to the documented algorithm allowlist. An operator or tooling bug could accidentally supply a P-384/P-521 key; it would be silently accepted rather than rejected with a clear "unsupported curve" error. `keys_test.go` has no test locking this down.

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit curve check in the `*ecdsa.PublicKey` case: reject any curve other than `elliptic.P256()` with a clear error message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ParsePublicKey` rejects ECDSA keys on curves other than P-256 with an explicit, clear error.
- [ ] Add a test: parse a valid ECDSA P-384 (or P-521) public key PEM and assert `ParsePublicKey` returns an error.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/keys.go:22-37`
- `pkg/audit/verify/keys_test.go`

title: Fix canonical JSON integer normalization (writeCanonicalNumber writes raw literal, not normalized value)
content:
## Problem

```go
// pkg/audit/verify/canonical.go:65-80
func writeCanonicalNumber(buf *strings.Builder, n json.Number) error {
    s := string(n)
    ...
    if _, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf(...)
    }
    buf.WriteString(s)   // writes the ORIGINAL string, not the parsed/normalized value
    return nil
}
```

This validates that `s` parses as an int64 but then writes the **original literal** rather than the normalized value. This breaks the documented "byte-identical to Python's `json.dumps`" contract for numerals that are syntactically valid JSON but not in canonical form. Concretely, `-0` is valid per RFC 8259 grammar (`-` + int, int can be `"0"`) and survives Go's `json.Decoder`, but Python's `json.dumps(json.loads("-0"))` → `"0"`, while this code emits `-0` verbatim.

## Verified

Confirmed by reading the code directly.

## Failure scenario

A bundle field legitimately containing `-0` (e.g. a hand-edited or re-serialized bundle) fails signature re-verification even though the underlying signed value is semantically `0` — a false negative (fails closed, not a forgery), but a real correctness bug. `canonical_test.go` has no negative-number test at all today.

## Suggested fix

```go
i, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)
if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf(...) }
buf.WriteString(strconv.FormatInt(i, 10))
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CanonicalJSONBytes` normalizes `-0` (and any other non-canonical-but-valid integer literal) to match Python `json.dumps` output byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Add a negative-integer test case, including `-0`, to `canonical_test.go`.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/canonical.go:65-80`
- `pkg/audit/verify/canonical_test.go`

title: Fix multi-record ("set") bundle CLI display bugs (root hint, Rekor log-index hint) and add test coverage
content:
## Problem

`formatRecordLine` is called for every record with the single global `result.SignedRoot` and the flattened `result.AnchorCmds`:

```go
// cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:78-81
for _, rec := range result.Records {
    fmt.Fprintln(w, formatRecordLine(rec, result.SignedRoot, result.AnchorCmds))
}
```

`Result.SignedRoot` is populated only in `verifySingleRecord` (nil for set bundles per its own doc comment), so the per-record `root=…` hint silently vanishes for every record in a set bundle. `Result.AnchorCmds` (merged from `anchor_refs_by_root` in `verifyMultiRecord`) is last-root-wins per anchor type, so a set with multiple roots each anchored to a different Rekor entry shows the *same* (only sometimes correct) `Rekor log-index=` on every record line, regardless of which root actually covers that record.

## Impact

Misleading diagnostic output for an auditor cross-referencing per-record evidence against an anchor. Entirely invisible to CI today — every fixture in `core_test.go` and `testdata/parity/*` is a single-record bundle; nothing exercises `verifyMultiRecord`/`Completeness` through `Run()`, even though `printResult` has dedicated set-bundle branches (`output.go:124-131`).

## Suggested fix

Either key `AnchorCmds` and a root hint per-record (by `root_id`) in the library (`pkg/audit/verify`), or have the CLI look up each record's own root (via `RecordResult`'s root reference, or by extending `RecordResult` to carry its `root_id`) before rendering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add at least one multi-record ("set") bundle test case that exercises `Run()` end-to-end (not just the library).
- [ ] Per-record display hints (`root=`, `Rekor log-index=`) are correct for each record's own root in a set bundle with multiple roots anchored differently.

- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core_test.go`

title: Deduplicate immudb/rekor anchor aggregation loops in verifyMultiRecord
content:
## Problem

The immudb block (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:541-567`) and the rekor block (`verify.go:569-595`) each iterate `anchorRefsByRoot` **twice**: once to compute `*AnyFail`, and — only if that came back `false` — again to find a representative `AnchorVerified`/`OK` result to attach to `Result.ImmudbResult`/`RekorResult`. `VerifyImmudbAnchor`/`VerifyRekorAnchor` are re-invoked on the same input the second time. Beyond the redundant work, the two ~25-line blocks are structurally identical apart from which verify function and result type they use.

## Impact

Not independently exploitable, but this is exactly the kind of duplicated logic that's easy to fix in one copy and miss in the other — see the linked `--require-anchor` bypass issue, whose fix touches both of these blocks; without deduplication that fix has to be applied twice.

## Suggested fix

Extract a small shared helper that collects per-root results once (e.g. iterating the authoritative root list per the linked bypass-fix issue), then derives both `anyFail` and "first success" from the cached results, parameterized over the verify function and result type (generics, or two thin wrappers around one shared loop).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Immudb and rekor aggregation share one implementation (no duplicated ~25-line block).
- [ ] Each anchor is verified at most once per root per `VerifyBundle` call (no redundant re-invocation).
- [ ] Should be implemented together with or immediately after [[i-696n]] (the require-anchor bypass fix), since that fix touches this same code.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:541-595`

title: Add missing security-relevant test coverage across verify.go edge cases
content:
## Problem

Several edge cases that the review specifically probed have no test coverage in `verify_test.go`:

- No test isolates `rangeContiguous` from the hash-chain check `innerOK` — i.e. a bundle where the root-to-root hash chain is genuinely intact (correct `prev_root_hash_b64` links) but `covered_range` spans have a real gap between two correctly-signed, correctly-chained roots (e.g. seq 0-1, then seq 4-5 with no batch for 2-3). Every existing multi-root "incomplete" test breaks the hash chain or the span endpoints, not an interior `covered_range` gap between otherwise-valid links.
- No test drives `FloorOK == nil` (e.g. an unparseable `retention_policy.mode`) through to `VerifyBundle` and asserts `ExitCode == 1`, despite the explicit "callers must treat nil as a failure, never as a silent pass" comment on `Result.FloorOK`.
- No test exercises the `RequireAnchor` bypass scenarios from [[i-696n]] (malformed/absent `anchor_refs_by_root`).

## Suggested fix

Add targeted regression tests for each of the three gaps above. These can be added alongside the corresponding fix issues ([[i-696n]] for the anchor bypass test) or as a standalone hardening pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interior `covered_range` gap test with an otherwise-intact hash chain, asserting `SetStatus == SetIncomplete`.
- [ ] `FloorOK == nil` → `ExitCode == 1` regression test.
- [ ] Tests for the `RequireAnchor` bypass scenarios (may be satisfied by tests added under [[i-696n]] instead of duplicating here).

feedback.content:
Added two of the three targeted regression tests to `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`:

- `TestVerifyBundleSetInteriorRangeGapWithIntactChain`: builds a two-root set bundle, widens root-1's `covered_range` to seq 4-5 (re-signed, since `covered_range` is in `SignableRootFields`) while leaving `prev_root_hash_b64`/`prev_root_id` untouched, and widens `completeness` to match so `spanOK` still passes. Asserts `ChainOK == ChainOK` (hash chain genuinely intact) and `SetStatus == SetIncomplete` (caught solely by `rangeContiguous`), isolating it from `innerOK`.
- `TestVerifyBundleFloorOKNilCausesExitCodeOne`: sets `retention_policy.mode` to an unparseable value (re-signed), drives it through `VerifyBundle`, and asserts `FloorOK == nil` and `ExitCode == 1`.

Deliberately did NOT add a `RequireAnchor` bypass test here: i-696n's underlying bug (iterating `anchor_refs_by_root`'s own keys instead of `signed_roots`) is still unfixed on this branch, so a test asserting `ExitCode != 0` for an absent/malformed `anchor_refs_by_root` map would fail against current code. Per this issue's own acceptance criteria ("may be satisfied by tests added under i-696n instead of duplicating here"), that regression test belongs with i-696n's fix commit, which lists the same two scenarios as its own acceptance criteria.

title: De-tautologize Merkle left/right sibling test coverage
content:
## Problem

`verify_test.go`'s `merkleProofFixture` builds every bundle-level test fixture's `audit_path` "left"/"right" strings directly from `InclusionProof`'s own `Side` output. That means `merkle_test.go`, `rekor_test.go`, and `verify_test.go` all validate proof generation and proof verification against **each other**, never against an independent expectation — a systematic left/right-swap bug in `InclusionProof` (or in `VerifyInclusion`'s consumption of `Side`) would be invisible across the entire suite. Only `TestMerkleTreeShapeKnownVector` hand-pins one branch (`SideLeft`, the odd-index/leaf-2-of-3 case); there's no equivalent hand-pinned `SideRight` case, and no test constructs an `audit_path` by hand (literal hash bytes + literal `"left"`/`"right"` strings) to exercise `VerifyMerkleInclusion` independently of `InclusionProof`.

Note: the tree-shape algorithm itself (`BuildTree`'s bottom-up pair-adjacent/promote-lone-odd-node construction) was independently hand-verified as mathematically equivalent to RFC 6962's recursive-split `MTH` definition for n=3,5,6 — this finding is specifically about test *independence* for the side-ordering logic, not the tree shape.

## Suggested fix

- Add a hand-pinned `SideRight` assertion (mirroring the existing `SideLeft` one in `TestMerkleTreeShapeKnownVector`).
- Add a test that builds `audit_path` by hand (literal bytes/strings, not derived from `InclusionProof`) and feeds it to `VerifyMerkleInclusion` directly.
- Add a "side-swap" tamper test: flip a valid proof step's `Side` while keeping its `Hash` unchanged, and assert `VerifyInclusion` rejects it — proving left/right ordering is cryptographically load-bearing rather than incidentally caught by existing wrong-hash/wrong-root/wrong-leaf tamper tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one hand-constructed (not `InclusionProof`-derived) test vector exercises `VerifyMerkleInclusion`/`VerifyInclusion` for both `SideLeft` and `SideRight`.
- [ ] A side-swap tamper test exists and fails against a hypothetical Left/Right-swapped `VerifyInclusion` implementation.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/merkle_test.go`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go` (`merkleProofFixture`)
- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor_test.go`

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED. `merkle_test.go:159-174` `TestMerkleTreeShapeKnownVectorSideRight` hand-pins a `SideRight` proof independent of `InclusionProof`'s own derivation (the explicit counterpart to the pre-existing `SideLeft` known-vector test). `merkle_test.go:182-200` `TestVerifyInclusionRejectsSideSwap` flips a valid step's `Side` and asserts rejection. `verify_test.go:991-1037` `TestVerifyMerkleInclusionHandConstructedAuditPath` builds node hashes directly from `leafNodeHash`/`nodeHash`, hand-writes literal `"left"`/`"right"` strings, and exercises both sides plus a bundle-level side-swap negative through the full `VerifyMerkleInclusion` path. Both acceptance criteria (independent vector + side-swap tamper test) met at primitive and bundle layers. Closing.

title: Fix verify.md algorithm step numbering to match doc.go's authoritative numbering
content:
## Problem

`pkg/audit/verify/doc.go` (lines 18-27) — the package's own authoritative godoc, explicitly cited by `verification-bundle-schema.md` as its source — numbers the 8 verification steps as: 1 leaf-hash, 2 signature, 3 Merkle, 4 root-signature, 5 root-chain continuity, 6 retention-floor, 7 rekor, 8 immudb. `verification-bundle-schema.md`'s steps 5-8 (lines ~132-290) are entirely different: 5 = confirm via live `rekor-cli`, 6 = MinIO/S3 confirmation, 7 = set-bundle completeness, 8 = offline rekor SET/inclusion/checkpoint. A reader trying to map "Step N" between the doc and the Go source (as the doc itself instructs: "This is the seed algorithm for the mpe verify Go implementation") will find the numbers refer to entirely different checks, making it impossible to cross-reference code comments (e.g. `// VerifyRootChain is Step 5...`) against the doc's Step 5 (a live rekor-cli shell command).

Renumber the markdown doc's steps to match `doc.go` (or vice versa), and give retention-floor and root-chain-continuity their own explicit steps in the markdown doc.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Step numbers in `verification-bundle-schema.md` match `pkg/audit/verify/doc.go`'s numbering exactly, 1:1.

title: Fully document immudb anchor_refs schema fields
content:
## Problem

The Full JSON Schema example and Field Reference in `verification-bundle-schema.md` (lines ~98, 314) show only `anchor_refs.immudb.tx_id` and `.database`. `VerifyImmudbAnchor` (`pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go:204-328`) — reachable via the documented `--immudb-public-key`/`--require-anchor immudb` flags — actually requires, across its three sub-checks (inclusion proof, state signature, ALH binding): `state_db`/`database`, `entry_hash`, `tx_eH`, `tx_nentries`, `tx_id`, `tx_hash`, `state_signature`, `inclusion_proof`, `tx_ts`, `tx_version`, `tx_bl_tx_id`, `tx_bl_root`, `tx_prev_alh`. An operator trying to understand what `--immudb-public-key` actually validates, or a bundle producer trying to know what to embed, has no documentation to go on — the doc implies immudb anchoring is as simple as a `tx_id`/`database` lookup, when it's actually a 3-part cryptographic proof (HTree inclusion + signed state + ALH binding).

## Suggested fix

Add an immudb Field Reference block and a "Step — immudb anchor verification" section mirroring the existing rekor one, listing all fields `VerifyImmudbAnchor` consumes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every field consumed by `VerifyImmudbAnchor` appears in the schema doc's Field Reference.

- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go:204-328` (ground truth)

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED ADDRESSED. Ground-truth field list from `VerifyImmudbAnchor`/`VerifyImmudbALHBinding` (`immudb.go:271-324`) — 13 fields (`state_db`/`database`, `entry_hash`, `tx_eH`, `tx_nentries`, `tx_id`, `tx_hash`, `state_signature`, `inclusion_proof`, `tx_ts`, `tx_version`, `tx_bl_tx_id`, `tx_bl_root`, `tx_prev_alh`) — all present in `verification-bundle-schema.md`'s Field Reference (`:433-445`) and JSON Schema example (`:116-128`). title: Fix errcheck lint violations and missing #nosec G304 annotations in cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify
content:

`golangci-lint run ./cmd/mpe/... ./pkg/audit/verify/...` reports unchecked `fmt.Fprintln`/`fmt.Fprintf` return values (errcheck) across `core.go` and `output.go` — more pervasive than a first pass suggests: `core.go:98,99,105,111,117,123,129,134,149` and effectively every `fmt.Fprint*` call in `output.go` (lines 80, 84, 86, 96, 99, 105, 107, 109, 116, 118, 120, 125-130, 134, 135, 142, 152). golangci-lint's default `errcheck` exclusions cover bare `fmt.Print*`/`os.Stdout.*` writes but not `fmt.Fprintln`/`fmt.Fprintf` against an arbitrary `io.Writer`.

content:

title: Make InclusionProof/Root return errors instead of panicking on invalid input
content:
## Problem

`InclusionProof(tree, leafIndex)` (`pkg/audit/verify/merkle.go:88-113`) does no bounds check on `leafIndex`: a negative index or an out-of-range index drives `sibIdx` negative/overflowing and panics on `level[sibIdx]` — an unrecovered slice-index panic, not a returned error. `Root(tree)` (`merkle.go:82-86`) similarly panics on an empty/nil `tree`. Every other exported primitive in this package (`b64Decode`, `ParsePublicKey`, byte-encoding helpers) returns an error on malformed input instead of panicking — these two exported functions are the outliers.

## Impact

Not reachable from untrusted bundle data today — `verify.go`'s `VerifyMerkleInclusion` (the actual untrusted-bundle verification path) never calls `InclusionProof`/`Root`; it consumes the bundle's own `audit_path` via `bundleAuditPath` + `VerifyInclusion`. Today `InclusionProof`/`BuildTree`/`Root` are used only by test fixture builders. Still worth hardening since these are exported package API and the panic-vs-error inconsistency is a real footgun for future callers (e.g. a future bundle-building CLI).

## Suggested fix

Add bounds/emptiness checks and return `(..., error)` from `InclusionProof`/`Root`, updating call sites (test helpers) accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `InclusionProof` returns an error (not a panic) for `leafIndex < 0` or `leafIndex >= len(tree[0])`.
- [ ] `Root` returns an error (not a panic) for an empty/nil `tree`.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/merkle.go:82-113`

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED. `pkg/audit/verify/merkle.go:85-106` — `Root(tree) ([]byte, error)` returns `fmt.Errorf(...)` on an empty tree/root level; `InclusionProof(tree, leafIndex) ([]ProofStep, error)` returns an error on empty tree and on `leafIndex < 0 || leafIndex >= len(tree[0])` *before* any indexing — no panic path remains in either function. Spot-checked directly (grep for `panic`/`return nil, fmt.Errorf` in merkle.go). Tests: `TestRootRejectsEmptyTree`, `TestInclusionProofRejectsOutOfRangeLeafIndex` (both boundaries). Note `BuildTree` still panics on empty input by design — out of this issue's scope, which names only `InclusionProof`/`Root`. Closing.

title: Tighten b64Decode alphabet-mixing and padding validation
content:
## Problem

`bytes.go`'s `b64Decode` unconditionally applies `strings.NewReplacer("-", "+", "_", "/")`, so a string mixing both standard and URL-safe alphabets (e.g. `"ab-c+d_e/f"`) is silently normalized and decoded rather than rejected. `b64CharsRe` (`^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*$`) also permits an unbounded run of trailing `=`, not capped at 2 as real base64 padding requires.

## Impact

Defense-in-depth only — in practice this is caught downstream by `base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString`'s own padding-shape validation (confirmed: truly malformed padding shapes like `"X==="` do error out), so it fails closed today. But the regex doesn't express the actual invariant, and the intentional "lenient" comment (mixing standard/URL-safe blobs) doesn't distinguish "either alphabet" from "both at once" within the same string.

## Suggested fix

Tighten `b64CharsRe`'s padding to `={0,2}`, and/or add an explicit check that a string doesn't simultaneously contain both `+`/`/` and `-`/`_` characters before normalizing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `b64Decode` rejects (or the regex correctly bounds) padding runs longer than 2.
- [ ] Add a test for a string mixing standard and URL-safe alphabet characters, asserting the desired behavior (reject, or document why lenient acceptance is intentional).

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/bytes.go`

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED. `pkg/audit/verify/bytes.go:63` bounds padding via `={0,2}` in `b64CharsRe`; `bytes.go:80-84` explicitly rejects mixed standard/URL-safe alphabets (`hasStd && hasURL` check) before normalizing. Tests `TestB64DecodeRejectsMixedAlphabet`, `TestB64DecodeRejectsOverlongPadding`, `TestB64DecodeAcceptsEitherAlphabet` all present in bytes_test.go. Closing.

- [ ] `getInt64Loose` no longer duplicates `getInt64`'s shared-type handling verbatim.

title: Minor consistency/doc nits: verifyMultiRecord error contract, retention-floor simplification doc, wire Usage() into --help
content:
## Problem (three small, related nits bundled together)

1. **Inconsistent error contract**: `verifyMultiRecord` never returns an `error`, unlike `verifySingleRecord` which errors on a structurally-broken bundle (missing `signed_root`). A multi-record bundle missing `signed_roots`/`records` entirely just silently fails closed via `ExitCode == 1` through the empty-map/`rootSigsOK` path rather than surfacing a distinguishable "malformed bundle" error like the single-record path does. Functionally safe (fails closed either way) but an inconsistent contract between `VerifyBundle`'s two dispatch branches. (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:388`, `681-691`)

2. **Undocumented simplification**: retention floor for multi-record sets is only evaluated against the earliest root's `retention_policy` (`sortedRoots[0]`), not per-root. This mirrors a known, documented limitation in the Clojure reference implementation, but the Go code has no comment calling this out as an intentional simplification — a future reader could reasonably assume per-root retention is enforced.

3. **Usage() not wired into --help**: the detailed exit-code table returned by `verify.Usage()` (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core.go:61-78`) is only ever printed on one specific error path (missing `--public-key`); it isn't set as `Description`/`UsageText` on the `cli.Command` in `main.go:241-246`, so `mpe verify --help`/`mpe help verify` never shows the exit-code convention operators need most.

## Suggested fix

1. Consider having `verifyMultiRecord` return an error for a bundle missing both `records` and `signed_roots` entirely (optional — low priority, since both paths already fail closed).
2. Add a one-line doc comment on the retention-floor code noting the earliest-root simplification is intentional.
3. Set `Description: verify.Usage()` (or `UsageText:`) when registering the `verify` subcommand in `main.go`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mpe verify --help` shows the exit-code table.
- [ ] Retention-floor-uses-earliest-root behavior has an explicit doc comment.
- [ ] (Optional) `verifyMultiRecord` surfaces a distinguishable error for a bundle missing both `records` and `signed_roots`.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:388,476-489,681-691`
- `cmd/mpe/main.go:241-246`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core.go:61-78`

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED ADDRESSED, all three sub-parts. (a) `verifyMultiRecord` now returns `(Result, error)` and surfaces a distinguishable error for a structurally broken bundle (`verify.go:484-486`), matching `verifySingleRecord`'s contract. (b) The retention-floor "evaluated only against the earliest root, not per-root" simplification is now an explicit code comment (`verify.go:586-589`) explaining it mirrors a documented limitation in the reference Clojure implementation, not an oversight. (c) `Usage()` is now wired as the subcommand's `Description` (`cmd/mpe/main.go:242-246`), so `mpe verify --help` renders the full exit-code table — previously it only printed on the missing-`--public-key` error path. Closing.

title: Bind the Rekor anchor to the bundle's own root hash
content:
## Problem

`VerifyRekorAnchor` (`pkg/audit/verify/rekor.go:251-321`) verifies the SET signature, the RFC 6962
inclusion proof, and checkpoint consistency — a fully self-consistent Rekor entry — but never checks
that `body_b64`'s artifact digest is *this bundle's* `signed_root.root_hash_b64`. The function isn't
even passed the bundle root. Same gap in `verify.go:363-364` (single-record call site) and
`verify.go:601-625`/`aggregateAnchorResults` (set-bundle call site).

I verified the true notary anchor format directly from `mpe-iam-lite@tamper-resistance`
(`notary/anchor/rekor.clj`, `notary/rekor/client.clj`): the notary anchors
`artifact = b64url_decode(signed_root.root_hash_b64)` as a `hashedrekord`, so a genuine entry's
`spec.data.hash.value` = `hex(sha256(root_hash_bytes))`. The notary itself already enforces this
binding at fetch/reuse time via `assert-entry-hash-matches!`/`entry-artifact-hash` — so this is a
well-defined, implementable offline check, not a guess.

## Failure scenario

An attacker (or a bug) copies *any genuine* Rekor entry for an unrelated artifact — real
`body_b64`/`set_b64`/`inclusion_proof`/`checkpoint`, validly signed by the real log key — into a
fraudulent or mismatched bundle's `anchor_refs.rekor`. `mpe verify --rekor-public-key ...
--require-anchor rekor` reports the bundle as anchored. The auditor concludes "this root is in the
public transparency log" when it is not.

## Suggested fix

1. Add `RekorEntryArtifactHashHex(bodyB64 string) (string, bool)` to `rekor.go`: decode `body_b64` as
   JSON and return `spec.data.hash.value` (lowercase hex).
2. Thread the bundle's `root_hash_b64` into `VerifyRekorAnchor` (new parameter). After the existing
   SET/inclusion/checkpoint checks pass, compute
   `expected = hex(sha256(b64Decode(rootHashB64)))` and require
   `strings.EqualFold(artifactHashHex, expected)`; on mismatch return `AnchorFailed` with a clear
   reason ("rekor entry artifact hash does not match this bundle's root").
3. Update call sites: single-record passes `signedRoot["root_hash_b64"]`; set-bundle's
   `aggregateAnchorResults` closure needs each root's own `signed_roots[id].root_hash_b64` threaded
   through (currently the closure only receives the anchor-refs map).
4. Tests: update `buildRekorFixture` (`rekor_test.go`) to build a real `hashedrekord` body whose
   `spec.data.hash.value` matches an intended root hash (parameterize the fixture on it). Add a
   regression test where a *valid* Rekor anchor for a *different* root FAILS — current fixtures
   structurally cannot catch this since `body_b64 = entries[logIndex]`, unrelated to any bundle root.
   Refresh `rekor-verified`/`rekor-failed` parity fixtures (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/testdata/`)
   accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `VerifyRekorAnchor` fails when the anchor's artifact hash doesn't match the bundle's own root
  hash, for both single-record and set bundles.
- [ ] Existing verified-anchor tests still pass with a correctly-bound fixture.
- [ ] New regression test: valid Rekor anchor bound to a *different* root → `AnchorFailed`.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor.go`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:363-364,601-625`
- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor_test.go`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/testdata/parity/rekor-verified/`, `rekor-failed/`

feedback.content:
Implemented. `VerifyRekorAnchor` now takes the bundle's `root_hash_b64` and, after the existing SET/inclusion-proof/checkpoint checks pass, decodes `body_b64` as a hashedrekord entry and requires `spec.data.hash.value == hex(sha256(root_hash_bytes))` (new `RekorEntryArtifactHashHex` helper in `rekor.go`), matching exactly what the notary anchors (`notary/anchor/rekor.clj`'s `artifact-bytes`/`build-hashedrekord`).

Call sites updated: `verifySingleRecord` passes `signedRoot["root_hash_b64"]`; `verifyMultiRecord`'s `aggregateAnchorResults` now passes each root's own id through to the verify closure so the rekor closure can look up that root's `signed_roots[id].root_hash_b64` (immudb's closure ignores it — no immudb binding yet, see `i-3bbv`).

Tests added in `rekor_test.go`:
- `TestVerifyRekorAnchorBoundToDifferentRootFails` — a fully valid anchor for root A fails against root B (the core regression this issue exists for).
- `TestVerifyRekorAnchorNonHashedrekordBodyFailsClosed` — a self-consistent entry whose body isn't a hashedrekord fails closed rather than skipping the check.
- Updated `buildRekorFixture` to accept an optional `bodyBytesOverride` (a real hashedrekord body bound to a chosen root hash, via new `hashedrekordBody` helper) so `TestVerifyRekorAnchorVerified`/`PromotedNodePath` exercise the full binding path; all other existing tests pass `nil` (unreached — they fail at earlier checks) and are otherwise unchanged.
- `verify_test.go`'s `TestVerifyBundleSetRequiredAnchorNonMapEntryFails` now binds its rekor fixture to root-1's actual `root_hash_b64` so it still tests what its comment says it tests.

One necessary, explicitly-documented exception: the golden `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/testdata/parity/rekor-verified` fixture is generated by the real Clojure `verify-bundle` CLI + a private rekor test key I don't have, and its `body_b64` is 32 arbitrary bytes (not a hashedrekord) — confirmed by decoding it. It structurally cannot pass the new binding check, and I can't regenerate it (no private key, no Clojure CLI here). Updated `parity_test.go`'s `rekor-verified` case to `expectedExit: 1`/`"rekor anchor: FAILED"` with a large comment explaining this is a known, tracked divergence from the (currently gapped) Clojure reference, not a regression — pending the mirrored fix in `notary/verify.clj` (tracked in `mpe-iam-lite` spec `s-xhch`'s companion note), at which point the fixture should be regenerated as a true bound hashedrekord and this case reverted to exit 0.

All package tests pass (`go test ./pkg/audit/verify/... ./cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/...`), `go vet`/`staticcheck`/`gofmt` clean.

title: immudb anchor cannot be bound to the bundle root offline — document limitation, block on notary fix
content:
## Problem

Same class of gap as [[i-H1a]] (see that issue), but for immudb — and **not fixable in this repo
alone**. `VerifyImmudbAnchor` (`pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go:204-328`) verifies HTree inclusion, the
signed `ImmutableState`, and ALH binding, but never checks that the anchored entry corresponds to
*this bundle's* `signed_root.root_hash_b64`.

I traced the notary source (`mpe-iam-lite@tamper-resistance`, `notary/anchor/immudb.clj`) to confirm
this genuinely cannot be fixed on the verifier side today: `entry_hash = sha256(sha256(root_id) ||
sha256(value))`, where `value = json/encode(signed_payload)` — cheshire's non-canonical JSON encoding
of the *full* signed payload, which still carries `root_pub_key_b64` (a field stripped before the
payload reaches the bundle proper). The offline verifier has no way to reproduce those exact bytes
from bundle-visible fields, so it cannot recompute or cross-check `entry_hash` against the root.

## Fix (this repo, now)

Do **not** fake a binding or weaken `--require-anchor immudb`'s pass/fail semantics. Instead:
- Reword the immudb `AnchorVerified` detail string (`immudb.go:326`) to state explicitly that offline
  immudb verification confirms inclusion + signed-state + ALH binding of *some* entry, but does
  **not** currently confirm that entry corresponds to this bundle's root.
- Update `docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md` Step 8 with the same caveat, so an
  operator relying on `--require-anchor immudb` isn't misled about what guarantee it provides today.

## Blocked on

Notary-side change tracked as its own spec in `mpe-iam-lite`: **`s-xhch` "Make immudb anchor
offline-verifiable against its bundle root"** (hand-injected into that repo's sudocode store per
