title: Set-bundle aggregate anchor line can print VERIFIED when some roots were only SKIPPED
content:
## Problem

For a set bundle, `Result.RekorResult`/`ImmudbResult` are set to `firstOK` from
`aggregateAnchorResults` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:601-625`) whenever no root's anchor *failed*.
If root-a is anchored and keyed (`AnchorVerified`) while root-b carries no anchor at all
(`AnchorSkipped`), the top-level transcript (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:111-131`) still
prints a blanket `rekor anchor: VERIFIED` / `immudb anchor: VERIFIED`, overstating coverage to an
auditor. It does not mask a genuine failure (a real failed root yields a synthetic `AnchorFailed`
result instead), and without `--require-anchor` a skip is legitimate for the exit code — so this is a
display-confidence issue, not a security bypass. `firstOK` is also chosen via Go's randomized map
iteration order, so which root's detail text is shown is nondeterministic run-to-run.

## Fix

`aggregateAnchorResults` already returns a `byRoot` map with every root's individual result — carry
that through to `Result` (it's currently discarded for immudb/rekor's summary construction) and
render a per-root summary, e.g. `VERIFIED (2 of 3 roots anchored; 1 skipped)`, instead of one
first-OK line. Consider a compact per-root breakdown if space allows.

Add a set-bundle test with a mix of anchored and un-anchored roots plus a supplied `--rekor-public-key`
(today's only set-bundle test supplies no anchor key at all, so this path is entirely untested).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Set-bundle anchor summary line reflects partial coverage instead of a nondeterministic
  first-OK line.
- [ ] New test: mixed anchored/un-anchored set bundle with a key supplied; assert the printed output
  does not claim full coverage.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:601-625`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:111-131`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core_test.go`

feedback.content:
Implemented. Added `anchorRootCounts` (verify.go) to tally verified/skipped/total from the `byRoot` map `aggregateAnchorResults` already returns. `verifyMultiRecord`'s immudb/rekor summary construction now branches on these counts instead of blindly taking `firstOK`:
- 0 verified anywhere → result stays `nil` (unchanged behavior).
- all roots verified → `Detail`/`Reason` says "verified for all N root(s)".
- some verified, some skipped (no failure) → "verified for N of M roots; K skipped" — the actual fix, so a mixed-coverage set bundle no longer reads as full coverage.
- any failure still wins first, unchanged.

Also fixed `output.go`: the rekor `AnchorVerified` branch previously printed a bare `"rekor anchor: VERIFIED"` and silently dropped `Reason` entirely, so even with the library fix the CLI would never have shown the new partial-coverage text. Now prints `Reason` when non-empty, unchanged (`"VERIFIED"` alone) when empty — preserves single-record bundles' existing output exactly.

Tests added:
- `TestVerifyBundleSetMixedAnchorCoverageReportsPartial` (verify_test.go) — library-level: root-0 gets a real, correctly-bound rekor anchor; root-1 has none; asserts `Reason` contains "1 of 2" and not "all 2".
- `TestPrintResult_RekorPartialCoverageSurfacesReason` (core_test.go) — CLI-rendering-level: confirms `printResult` surfaces a populated `Reason` and confirms the plain-VERIFIED (empty `Reason`) case is unchanged.

`go build ./...`, `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `gofmt -l` all clean; full `pkg/audit/verify` + `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify` suites pass.

title: canonical.go escapes U+007F incorrectly relative to its stated Python parity contract
content:
## Problem

`writeCanonicalString` (`pkg/audit/verify/canonical.go:144`) has `case r < 0x80: buf.WriteRune(r)`,
writing U+007F (DEL) raw. But the function's own documented contract is "byte-identical to Python's
`json.dumps(v, ..., ensure_ascii=True)`", and Python escapes DEL as ``:

```
$ python3 -c "import json; print(repr(json.dumps(chr(0x7f))))"
'"\\u007f"'
$ python3 -c "import json; print(repr(json.dumps(chr(0x7e))))"
'"~"'
```

(Verified directly — 0x7e is raw, 0x7f is escaped in Python's output.) This canonicalization is used
for the signed root-payload (`verify.go:156`, `VerifyRootSignature`) and the Rekor SET payload
(`rekor.go:65`).

## Impact

Fail-closed (a legitimate bundle field containing a literal DEL byte would produce mismatched
canonical bytes and a false verification *rejection*, not a forgery). Low real-world likelihood, but
a genuine parity bug relative to the stated contract.

## Suggested fix

Change `case r < 0x80:` to `case r < 0x7f:` so 0x7f falls through to the `\uXXXX` escape branch. Add
a canonical-JSON test asserting `""` output for a U+007F input string (alongside the existing
non-ASCII escape tests).

Also worth checking: does the notary's own signing-side canonicalizer use the same 0x7f/0x80
boundary? If it diverges, the notary needs the matching fix — file as a follow-up in `mpe-iam-lite`
if so, rather than duplicating a spec here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CanonicalJSONBytes` escapes U+007F as ``, matching Python's `json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True)`.
- [ ] Test vector added for U+007F (and confirms U+007E remains unescaped).

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/canonical.go:144`
- `pkg/audit/verify/canonical_test.go`

feedback.content:
Investigated further and the original finding was WRONG — reversed course rather than ship a regression. Correcting the record here.

The issue as filed assumed the Go verifier must match literal Python `json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True)` semantics (which does escape U+007F/DEL). But the actual invariant that matters is matching what the **notary signs**, not idealized Python behavior. I decompiled `mpe-iam-lite`'s actual signing dependency (`notary/canonical.clj` configures Jackson's `JsonWriteFeature.ESCAPE_NON_ASCII` on a `JsonGenerator`) and confirmed via `CharTypes.sOutputEscapes128`'s static initializer bytecode: index 127 (DEL) is never assigned a non-zero entry, so it defaults to 0 ("no escape"). `ESCAPE_NON_ASCII` only affects code points ≥ 0x80, so **Jackson — and therefore the real notary — never escapes DEL, writing it raw**, contrary to its own doc comment's "match Python ensure_ascii=True" claim.

This means the *original* Go code (`case r < 0x80:`, leaving DEL raw) was already correct and already matched the real signer. My initial "fix" (escaping DEL to match literal Python semantics) would have made the Go verifier reject a legitimately-signed bundle field containing a raw DEL byte — a real regression, caught before merge by actually testing the change against `go test`, and by not stopping at "matches the doc comment" without verifying the actual signer behavior.

**Resolution:** reverted the code change; kept and expanded the code comment on `writeCanonicalString` to explain precisely why DEL is left raw (matching Jackson's real behavior, not idealized Python parity) and to head off a future well-intentioned regression. Renamed/corrected the test to `TestCanonicalJSONBytesLeavesDELRaw` (asserts DEL passes through unescaped) plus `TestCanonicalJSONBytesLeavesTildeRaw` (sanity check on the 0x7f/0x80 boundary from the other side). No production behavior change — this issue closes as "investigated, no code fix needed; doc comment clarified in Go" rather than "bug fixed."

Note for awareness (not worth its own notary-side spec given the vanishingly low real-world likelihood — no signed field is realistically going to contain a literal DEL byte): `notary/canonical.clj`'s own doc comment has the identical Python-parity overclaim for DEL as Go's did. Purely cosmetic/doc-accuracy there, not a functional bug, since the *real* Clojure verifier and Go verifier now agree with each other and with what's actually signed.

`go build`, `gofmt -l`, `staticcheck`, and the full `pkg/audit/verify` suite all pass.

title: Chain-link check treats two absent hash fields as a vacuous match
content:
## Problem

`VerifyRootChain` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:200-207`) computes
`hashMatch := curPrevHash == prevRootHash` from two `getString` calls that both default to `""` on a
missing field. If both `prev_root_hash_b64` (current root) and `root_hash_b64` (predecessor root) are
absent, `"" == ""` is vacuously true and the chain link is reported as matching. The same pattern
exists in `verifyMultiRecord`'s inner chain-walk loop (`verify.go:566-568`).

## Impact

Not currently exploitable: this branch is only reached after `prevSigOK` (the predecessor's root
signature must independently verify), and both `root_hash_b64` and `prev_root_hash_b64` are members
of `SignableRootFields`, so a validly-signed root missing them shouldn't occur in practice. This is a
latent fail-open that would only bite if the notary's signed-field set ever changed.

## Suggested fix

Require non-empty before treating equality as a valid link:
`hashMatch := curPrevHash != "" && curPrevHash == prevRootHash`. Ideally decode-and-compare the actual
bytes (base64) rather than raw strings, so a std/url-safe encoding difference doesn't cause a spurious
mismatch either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two roots both missing their respective hash fields no longer report `ChainOK`.
- [ ] Regression test added for this specific case.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:200-207,566-568`

feedback.content:
Implemented. Two fixes in `verify.go`:
- `VerifyRootChain` (single-record path): `hashMatch := curPrevHash != "" && curPrevHash == prevRootHash` instead of a bare `==`.
- `verifyMultiRecord`'s inner chain-walk loop (set-bundle path, same pattern inverted): `if prevHash == "" || prevHash != nextPrevHash { innerOK = false ... }`.

Tests added: `TestVerifyBundleRootChainBothHashesAbsentFailsClosed` (single-record, via `prev_signed_root` with the predecessor's `root_hash_b64` stripped and re-signed) and `TestVerifyBundleSetInnerChainVacuousMatchFailsClosed` (two-root set bundle, root-0's `root_hash_b64` stripped + root-1's `prev_root_hash_b64` stripped, both re-signed). Both assert `ChainFailed`.

Verified these are real regressions, not tautologies: temporarily reverted just the two fixed lines back to the buggy `==`/`!=` form and confirmed both new tests fail against it, then restored and confirmed they pass against the fix.

`go build`, `gofmt -l`, `staticcheck`, and the full `pkg/audit/verify` + `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify` suites all pass.

title: ParseDuration silently overflows on multiply/sum
content:
## Problem

`ParseDuration`'s `toMs` closure (`pkg/audit/verify/retention.go:52-69`) only returns an error when a
single duration component's digit string doesn't fit `int64` via `strconv.ParseInt`. It does not
guard the subsequent `n * unit` multiplication or the running `total` sum, both of which silently
wrap on overflow (Go has no overflow trap) — e.g. `ParseDuration("P9999999999Y")` overflows `int64`
and wraps to a garbage (possibly negative) value with `err == nil`. This directly contradicts the
function's own comment ("surface it rather than silently treating ... as 0, which would understate
the parsed duration and could misjudge the retention floor").

## Impact

Limited: `floorOK` (`retention.go:117-130`) only affects `VerifyBundle`'s exit code through its `nil`
(parse-error) state, not its true/false value — so this bug alone cannot flip a bundle to a false
"verified." Still a real correctness gap worth hardening, since retention-floor evaluation directly
gates whether an absent record reads as "authorized-absent" vs. a tamper signal.

## Suggested fix

Use checked arithmetic for each `n * unit` and the running total — e.g. a pre-division bound check
(`n > math.MaxInt64 / unit`) or `math/bits.Mul64` — returning the existing "out of range" error path
instead of wrapping silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A duration component whose value fits `int64` but whose `n * unit` product overflows returns an
  error instead of a wrapped value.
- [ ] Regression test with an overflowing-product duration string (e.g. very large year count).

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/retention.go:52-69`
- `pkg/audit/verify/retention_test.go`

feedback.content:
Implemented. `ParseDuration`'s `toMs` closure now returns `(int64, error)` and checks `n > math.MaxInt64/unit` before the multiply (guarding the product); the summation loop now checks `total > math.MaxInt64-v` before each add (guarding the running sum) instead of one unchecked `+`-chain expression. Both surface the existing "out of range" error style rather than wrapping silently.

Tests added:
- `TestParseDurationRejectsOverflowingProduct` — `P9999999999Y`: the component fits int64 on its own (unlike the existing digit-run-too-long test) but its product with the year-unit overflows.
- `TestParseDurationRejectsOverflowingSum` — `P150000000YT1306000000000H`: computed precisely so each of Y (~4.73e18 ms) and H (~4.70e18 ms) individually stays under `math.MaxInt64` (~9.223e18), but their sum (~9.43e18) overflows.

Verified both are real regressions: temporarily reverted `retention.go` to the pre-fix version and confirmed both new tests fail against it, then restored and confirmed they pass.

`go build`, `gofmt -l`, `staticcheck`, and the full `pkg/audit/verify` + `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify` suites all pass.

title: Add an overall verdict line so "complete"/exit code never look contradictory
content:
## Problem

A verified record with an unparseable `retention_policy` yields `SetStatus = SetComplete`
(`verify.go:366-376` intentionally excludes `FloorOK == nil` from its `tampered` computation) while
`VerifyBundle` separately sets `ExitCode = 1` for the same case (`verify.go:767`). This is internally
consistent by design — retention-parse failures gate the exit code but not `SetStatus` — but the
printed transcript (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:133-140`) shows "Result set: complete"
right next to (elsewhere-printed) `Retention floor: ERROR`, and a script/operator skimming only the
"complete" line and the exit code sees a contradiction with no single line resolving it.

## Suggested fix

Print one trailing overall-verdict line derived directly from `result.ExitCode`, e.g.
`RESULT: FAILED (exit 1)` / `RESULT: OK`, so the exit code is never ambiguous relative to the
per-check lines above it. This doesn't require changing `SetStatus`'s semantics — just adds an
unambiguous summary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `printResult` emits a final verdict line matching `result.ExitCode`.
- [ ] Test asserts the verdict line is consistent across verified / tampered / unsealed /
  unparseable-retention fixtures.

## Files

- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:133-140`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core_test.go`

feedback.content:
Implemented. Added `verdictLine(exitCode int) string` in `output.go`, mapping `Result.ExitCode`'s documented convention to `"RESULT: OK (exit 0)"` / `"RESULT: UNVERIFIED (exit 2)"` / `"RESULT: FAILED (exit N)"` (default for 1 and any unexpected value). `printResult` now prints this as the final line, always.

Tests: extended `TestCrossImplementationParity`'s existing per-fixture loop (verified/tampered/unsealed/rekor-verified/rekor-failed — spanning exit codes 0, 1, 2) to also assert `stdout` contains `verdictLine(code)`. Also extended `TestRun_UnparseableRetentionPolicyExitsOneWithExplanation` — the exact scenario this issue is about ("Result set: complete" next to exit 1) — to assert both `"Result set: complete"` and `"RESULT: FAILED (exit 1)"` appear together, resolving the ambiguity this issue flagged.

`go build`, `gofmt -l`, `staticcheck`, and the full `pkg/audit/verify` + `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify` suites all pass.

title: Fix bundle-type dispatch ambiguity — tampered set data smuggled alongside a genuine single record reports VERIFIED
content:
## Problem

`VerifyBundle` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:793`, pre-fix) dispatched single-vs-set purely on the
presence of a top-level `"record"` key, with no check that the set-shaped keys (`"records"`,
`"signed_roots"`) were absent. `verifySingleRecord` never inspected `records`/`signed_roots`.
Bundle input is fully attacker-controlled.

## Failure scenario

Take any legitimately-signed single-record bundle (valid `record`, `signed_root`, `merkle_proof`).
Merge into the same JSON object a tampered `"records": [...]` array plus `"signed_roots": {...}`
containing forged/altered records. `VerifyBundle` sees `"record"` present → routes to
`verifySingleRecord`, which validates only the genuine single record and **ignores the entire
tampered set payload**. Result: `SetComplete` → `ExitCode 0`. A downstream consumer reading the
`records` array from the same "verified" file consumes tampered data. A weaker variant
(`record: null` + a stray valid `signed_root`) downgrades a genuinely-tampered set bundle from exit 1
to exit 2 ("no sealed records"), also masking tampering.

## Fix (applied)

Added a mutual-exclusion guard at the top of `VerifyBundle`: a bundle carrying `"record"` alongside
`"records"` or `"signed_roots"` is now rejected with an error before dispatch (CLI maps this to exit
3, "bundle parse / key load error" — already the correct bucket per `Usage()`'s documented
convention). Routing now only happens on exclusive presence.

## Verification

- New tests in `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`: `TestVerifyBundleAmbiguousShapeRejected`,
  `TestVerifyBundleAmbiguousShapeWithSignedRootsRejected`,
  `TestVerifyBundleAmbiguousShapeNullRecordRejected` (covers the `record: null` variant too).
- Full suite green under `go test` and `-race`; `go vet`/`staticcheck`/`gosec`/`golangci-lint` clean.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go` (`VerifyBundle`, ~line 793)

title: Bound CLI file reads with the same memory cap stdin already honors
content:
## Problem

`maxInputBytes` (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core.go:167`) is documented as "defense in depth
against an accidental (or adversarial) multi-gigabyte input exhausting memory." The **stdin** branch
of `loadBundle` honored this correctly via `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(os.Stdin, maxInputBytes+1))`.
But both **file** branches (`loadPublicKeyFile`, and `loadBundle`'s file branch) used
`os.ReadFile(path)`, which reads the entire file into memory *before* comparing `len(data)` against
the cap — the cap rejected the input only after the allocation it was meant to prevent had already
happened.

## Failure scenario

`mpe verify -k key.pem -b /path/to/50GB.json` (or a FIFO/`/dev/zero`-backed path, or a symlink to a
huge file) drove the process to allocate the full file size and could OOM before the
"exceeds ... byte limit" check ever ran. Piping the same bytes via stdin was safely rejected — an
inconsistent and surprising asymmetry. The existing tests masked this: they shrink `maxInputBytes`
below a small fixture, confirming rejection logic works but never exercising the large/unbounded-input
memory path.

## Fix (applied)

Added `readCappedFile(path)` in `core.go`: opens the file and reads through
`io.LimitReader(f, maxInputBytes+1)`, exactly mirroring stdin's bounded-read pattern. Both
`loadPublicKeyFile` and `loadBundle`'s file branch now go through it instead of `os.ReadFile`.

## Verification

- New regression test `TestRun_UnboundedFifoInputDoesNotHang` (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core_unix_test.go`,
  `//go:build !windows`): writes far more than `maxInputBytes+1` bytes into a FIFO without ever
  closing the writer end, and asserts `loadBundle` still returns (rejecting the oversized input)
  within a bounded time — proving the read is capped by byte count, not by waiting for EOF.
- Full suite green under `go test` and `-race`; `go vet`/`staticcheck`/`gosec`/`golangci-lint` clean.

title: Surface a tail-completeness caveat for set bundles — completeness.to_seq is unsigned and self-asserted
content:
## Problem

`completeness` is a top-level bundle field, **not** covered by `SignableRootFields` and thus not
covered by any signature. `verifyMultiRecord`'s `spanOK` check only validates the bundle's own roots
against this attacker-controllable range. There is a predecessor-side caveat (`ChainCaveat`/
`outerCaveat`, for when the first root claims a predecessor outside the bundle) but no analogous
caveat for a missing *successor*.

## Failure scenario

Set bundle with signed roots R1←R2←R3. An attacker removes R3 and its records, and sets
`completeness.to_seq = R2.to_seq`. `innerOK` (chain links), `rangeContiguous`, `spanOK`, and
`densityOK` all still hold → `SetComplete` → exit 0. The newest audit records are silently dropped
with zero signal to the operator. (Interior removal is already caught by chain-link verification;
only tail-truncation is exposed — this is partly inherent to offline verification, since there is no
authoritative "current head" without a live/anchor check, but the asymmetry with the documented
predecessor caveat meant the tool gave *no* signal at all.)

## Fix (applied)

Added `Result.TailUnverifiable`, always `true` for a set-bundle verification pass (regardless of
whether that pass reached `SetComplete`), documenting that offline verification can confirm the
bundle's own extent is internally consistent but can never rule out records dropped past its own
tail. `printResult` now emits a corresponding `Note:` line whenever it's set. `verify.md`'s Output
section documents the caveat alongside the sample output.

## Verification

- New tests: `TestVerifyBundleSetAlwaysReportsTailUnverifiable`,
  `TestVerifyBundleSingleRecordNeverReportsTailUnverifiable` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`);
  `TestRun_SetBundleSurfacesTailUnverifiableCaveat` (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core_test.go`,
  asserts the note appears for a set bundle and is absent for a single-record bundle).
- Full suite green under `go test` and `-race`; `go vet`/`staticcheck`/`gosec`/`golangci-lint` clean.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go` (`Result.TailUnverifiable`, `verifyMultiRecord`)
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go` (`printResult`)
- `docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`, `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core_test.go`

title: Correct immudb godoc/schema-doc overclaim of rekor-equivalent root binding
content:
## Problem

`immudb.go`'s godoc for `VerifyImmudbAnchor`/`VerifyImmudbRootBinding` (and the parallel prose in
`verification-bundle-schema.md`) stated that immudb's Part 4 root-hash check "mirrors the rekor
artifact-hash binding check" / is "the same class of fix, closing the equivalent gap." This
equivalence is false in a security-relevant way: rekor's artifact hash lives *inside* the SET-signed
`body_b64` (`VerifyRekorSET` verifies the log's signature over a payload that includes it) — an
attacker cannot repoint it without forging the log's signature. immudb's `root_binding_hash` is a
plain field in `anchor_refs.immudb` that **no signature in the chain commits to**: the state
signature covers `(db, tx_id, tx_hash)`, the ALH commits `tx_hash → tx_eH`, and inclusion binds
`entry_hash → tx_eH` — but nothing binds `root_binding_hash` to the bundle root. Part 4 therefore only
catches *accidental* mismatch, not adversarial substitution (this is the same underlying limitation
round 2 already tracks in `i-H1b`; this issue is about the *documentation* falsely claiming that
limitation was closed, not the limitation itself).

## Impact

The docs told a future maintainer immudb has the same tamper-resistance as rekor, inviting either
dropping a compensating out-of-band control or advertising immudb-anchored bundles as equivalently
trustworthy.

## Fix (applied)

Reworded all affected doc comments/prose (`immudb.go`'s `VerifyImmudbAnchor` doc, `VerifyImmudbRootBinding`
doc, and the Part-4 inline comment; `verification-bundle-schema.md`'s check-4 prose, the
`anchor_refs.immudb.root_binding_hash` field-reference row, and the 1.1.4 changelog entry) to state
plainly that `root_binding_hash` is an *unsigned notary assertion* verified only for internal
consistency, not committed to by any signature in the offline proof — and to stop calling it
equivalent to the rekor check.

## Verification

Documentation-only change; `go build`/`go vet` confirm no code behavior changed (godoc comments
don't affect compilation). Read back all edited passages to confirm no other doc claims the same
equivalence.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go` (3 doc-comment locations)
- `docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md` (3 locations: check-4 prose, field table, changelog)

title: Reject non-well-formed UTF-8 in canonical-JSON string encoding instead of silently collapsing to U+FFFD
content:
## Problem

`writeCanonicalString` (`pkg/audit/verify/canonical.go`) ranged over its input with
`for _, r := range s`, which silently substitutes U+FFFD for each invalid UTF-8 byte. Separately,
`encoding/json` maps an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escape (e.g. `\uD800`) to U+FFFD at decode time.
So a raw invalid byte, a lone surrogate escape, and a genuine literal U+FFFD could all canonicalize
to identical bytes — two distinct signed-field values producing the same canonical-JSON encoding.

## Impact

Bounded: the signature-relevant root fields (`root_hash_b64`, `tree_size`, `prev_root_hash_b64`,
etc.) are ASCII/base64/numeric, so a *tamper-accept* forgery via this path was not reachable. The
realistic effect was the opposite — a false *rejection* (availability issue) of a legitimately-signed
free-form field containing a lone surrogate, since the verifier's canonical reconstruction would
differ from what the Jackson-based signer actually produced (which does emit literal `\udXXX` for
unpaired surrogates, matching Jackson's own behavior, not Python's `ensure_ascii` idealization — the
same "match the actual signer" principle already applied to DEL handling per `i-7j0j`).

## Fix (applied)

`writeCanonicalString` now checks `utf8.ValidString(s)` up front and returns an error for
non-well-formed input, rather than silently substituting U+FFFD. Threaded `error` returns through
`writeCanonical`'s string case and `writeCanonicalMap`'s key-encoding call site (both previously
called it as a `void` function).

## Verification

- New tests: `TestCanonicalJSONBytesRejectsInvalidUTF8`, `TestCanonicalJSONBytesRejectsInvalidUTF8Key`,
  `TestCanonicalJSONBytesAcceptsGenuineReplacementCharacter` (confirms a legitimately-encoded U+FFFD
  still round-trips and is not rejected) — `pkg/audit/verify/canonical_test.go`.
- Full suite green under `go test` and `-race`; `go vet`/`staticcheck`/`gosec`/`golangci-lint` clean.

## Known residual limitation

This only catches malformed bytes reaching `writeCanonicalString` directly. A lone UTF-16 surrogate
escape in the original bundle JSON is already collapsed to a valid-UTF-8-encoded U+FFFD by
`encoding/json`'s decoder before `DecodeBundle`'s output ever reaches this function — recovering that
distinction would require a custom JSON string decoder, out of scope for this defense-in-depth check.
Documented inline in `writeCanonicalString`'s doc comment.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/canonical_test.go`

title: Recompute immudb entry_hash from bundle's own signed_root + root_id; retire root_binding_hash
content:
## Problem

`VerifyImmudbAnchor`'s Part 4 (`pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go`) currently checks
`root_binding_hash == sha256(b64url_decode(root_hash_b64))` — an unsigned field covered by no
signature, so it only catches accidental mismatch, not a genuine-but-unrelated immudb anchor
deliberately paired with a forged bundle (see [[i-7xbs]]). `entry_hash` itself — the value actually
carried through immudb's real proof chain (inclusion proof → `tx_eH` → signed `tx_hash`) — is read
straight from the bundle and never independently recomputed or cross-checked against anything.

## Design

Recompute the expected `entry_hash` from data the verifier already trusts, reusing the exact
machinery `VerifyRootSignature` already uses for the root signature:

```go
expectedValueBytes := CanonicalJSONBytes(selectKeys(signedRoot, SignableRootFields))
expectedEntryHash := sha256(concat(sha256(rootIDBytes), sha256(expectedValueBytes)))
// require expectedEntryHash == b64Decode(anchor_refs.immudb.entry_hash)
```

This mirrors immudb's own `entry_hash = sha256(sha256(key) || sha256(value))` shape (`key = root_id`,
`value` = the canonically-encoded signable-fields subset of the signed root, once the notary-side
change lands — see this issue's parent spec [[s-16qk]] for the cross-repo dependency).

## Dependency

Requires the companion notary-side change (tracked in `mpe-iam-lite`, not this repo): the immudb
anchor value must be stored as `canonical-json-bytes(select-keys(signed-payload, signable-root-fields))`
instead of today's non-canonical full-payload encoding, and `root_id` must be present on the bundle.
**Single-record bundles carry no `root_id` today** (confirmed by reading `notary/bundle.clj`'s
`assemble-record-bundle` — `root-id` is used only internally, never serialized); set bundles already
expose it as the `signed_roots`/`anchor_refs_by_root` map keys, so no bundle-schema change is needed
for that path. `DecodeBundle`/`verifySingleRecord` will need to read the new field once the notary
ships it.

Per explicit user direction, no backward compatibility with anchors written before the cutover is
required — `root_binding_hash` should be removed outright, not kept as a fallback.

## Proposed change

- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go`: replace `VerifyImmudbRootBinding` (and the `root_binding_hash` field
  parsing in `VerifyImmudbAnchor`'s Part 4) with the `entry_hash` recomputation above. Remove
  `root_binding_hash` handling entirely — no fallback path.
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`: thread `root_id` through to `VerifyImmudbAnchor`'s call site for the
  single-record path (`verifySingleRecord`) once the bundle carries it; the set-bundle path
  (`verifyMultiRecord`/`aggregateAnchorResults`) already has `id` (the root's map key) available in
  its closure and can pass it straight through.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A genuine immudb anchor for root A, paired with a bundle claiming a *different* root B (same
  attack shape as the already-fixed Rekor case), now fails verification instead of passing.
- [ ] A genuine, matching immudb anchor still verifies correctly (no false rejection).
- [ ] `root_binding_hash` field, parsing, and doc references are fully removed — not deprecated,
  removed.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`
- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb_test.go`, `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`

## Related

- [[s-16qk]] (parent spec, full design + cross-repo context)
- [[i-7xbs]] (this repo, closed — docs-only fix this supersedes with the real cryptographic fix)

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-17): CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED at HEAD (`0101f2f`, unchanged since). `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go:165-198` — `expectedImmudbEntryHash` computes `sha256(sha256(root_id) || sha256(CanonicalJSONBytes(selectKeys(signed_root, SignableRootFields))))` exactly per [[s-16qk]]'s design; `VerifyImmudbEntryHash` decodes `anchor_refs.immudb.entry_hash` and requires equality. Threaded through both call sites: single-record (`verify.go:395-396`) and set-bundle (`verify.go:657-660`, per-root `id`/`sr`). `root_binding_hash` is retired — grep across the repo shows it survives only in two doc-comments (`immudb.go:182,243`) narrating what was superseded; no parsing/verification code references it. Fails closed (not skipped) when `entry_hash` is present but `root_id`/`signed_root` are unavailable. Regression test `TestVerifyImmudbAnchorBoundToDifferentRootFails` (immudb_test.go:143) plus fail-closed twins and the happy path are present. Closing — no further action needed; this repo's half of [[s-16qk]] is done (the doc-side issue [[i-h9bz]] and test-side [[i-8vz7]] were already closed separately, and [[i-1cpa]] remains blocked on the cross-repo notary fixture as its own feedback documents).

title: Set-bundle disclosed records not counted against signed tree_size — interior redaction passes as SetComplete
content:
## Problem

For a multi-record ("set") bundle, `verifyMultiRecord` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`) never
cross-checks that the disclosed `records` entries actually cover every leaf the root's own **signed**
`tree_size` claims to contain. Specifically:

- `densityOK` (verify.go ~767) only checks `tree_size >= to_seq - from_seq + 1` — a property of the
  root's own signed metadata, independent of what was disclosed.
- `allVerified` (verify.go ~714) ranges only over the `records` that happen to be present; it is
  vacuously true when some are simply missing.
- `spanOK` / `rangeContiguous` compare only root **endpoints** against `completeness.from_seq/to_seq`.
- `completeness.total_records` is carried in the schema and set by fixtures but is **read nowhere** in
  `verify.go` (grep-confirmed).
- There is no check that the `merkle_proof.leaf_index` values seen for a given root form a complete,
  duplicate-free covering of `[0, tree_size)`.

Bundle input is fully attacker-controlled (per `doc.go`'s threat model). The signed `tree_size` is
sufficient evidence to detect an interior drop, but it is never used for a leaf-coverage count.

## Failure scenario (empirically reproduced)

Using the repo's own `buildSetBundle` test helper (batch 0 = root-0 with signed `tree_size=2`
covering seq 0–1, two records r0/r1), delete record r1 (leaf 1 of the tree_size=2 batch) and call
`VerifyBundle`. Observed result:

```
records disclosed=3, SetStatus="complete", ExitCode=0
  record status="verified"
  record status="verified"
  record status="verified"
```

A genuine, correctly-signed, correctly-chained audit trail with one record silently redacted from a
batch is certified **complete / exit 0**. Every disclosed record's signature and Merkle proof is
authentic; the missing one is simply never accounted for. A downstream consumer or operator relying
on `SetComplete` to certify the full trail for the covered range is misled.

## Impact

HIGH. This is the "reports verified for something unproven" failure the verifier exists to prevent.
Distinct from prior findings:
- **not** `i-4mfr` (closed): that density check compares `tree_size` against the `covered_range`
  span, not against the count of disclosed leaves.
- **not** `i-2ldg` (closed): that caveat covers the **unsigned tail** (`completeness.to_seq` being
  self-asserted, i.e. records dropped *past* the bundle's end). This gap is an **interior** drop
  *within* a cryptographically-signed `tree_size`.

`doc.go`'s claim that completeness is "derived from cryptographic evidence … rather than trusting the
bundle's self-asserted `completeness.contiguous` flag" is therefore an overstatement for the
per-record disclosure dimension and should be corrected alongside the fix.

## Suggested fix

For each `root_id` in `signed_roots`, collect the `leaf_index` values among the `records` that
reference it and require they are distinct and exactly cover `{0, …, tree_size-1}` (at minimum,
`count(records-for-root) == tree_size`) before allowing `derivedContiguous` / `SetComplete` for that
root. This also gives `completeness.total_records` a real cross-check role. Narrow the `doc.go`
wording to match whatever guarantee the fixed code actually provides.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A set bundle that drops any record from an otherwise dense/signed/chained root no longer reports
      `SetComplete`; it reports an incomplete/failed status with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Per-root leaf coverage is checked: disclosed `leaf_index` values are distinct and cover
      `[0, tree_size)`; duplicates or gaps fail closed.
- [ ] A regression test in `verify_test.go` builds a `buildSetBundle`-style bundle with one record
      dropped and asserts the failure (this test must fail against the current implementation).
- [ ] `doc.go`'s completeness claim is aligned with the implemented guarantee.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go` (`verifyMultiRecord`, ~714 and ~767–792)
- `pkg/audit/verify/doc.go` (completeness claim, ~30–33)
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go` (new regression test)

feedback.content:
Implemented the per-root leaf-coverage check (i-8sjb):

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`: added `leafIndicesCoverTree` and a new `coverageOK` check in `verifyMultiRecord`, gating `derivedContiguous`/`SetComplete`. For each signed root, the disclosed `merkle_proof.leaf_index` values must be distinct and exactly cover `[0, tree_size)`; a missing `tree_size`, a gap, or a duplicate all fail closed. Also cross-checks `completeness.total_records` (previously read nowhere) against the sum of signed `tree_size` values across roots.
- `pkg/audit/verify/doc.go`: package doc now describes per-root leaf-index coverage as part of the completeness derivation.
- `docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md`: "Verify completeness" section now documents 5 checks (added check 5), and the `completeness.total_records` field-reference row reflects its new cross-check role.
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go`: added `TestVerifyBundleSetDroppedRecordFailsCoverage` (reproduces the exact failure scenario from the issue — dropping r1 from a `buildSetBundle`-style bundle) and `TestVerifyBundleSetDuplicateLeafIndexFailsCoverage` (a cloned leaf_index that keeps the disclosed count matching tree_size while a real leaf goes uncovered). Verified both tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass after the fix. Full repo test suite (`go test ./...`) and `go vet` pass.

title: Non-numeric --trusted-now exits 1 (TAMPERED code), not documented exit 3
content:
## Problem

The documented exit-code contract (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core.go` `Usage()`, and
`docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md:96`) states exit 3 = "bundle parse / key load error / invalid flag
value". But `--trusted-now` is an `Int64Flag`, so a non-numeric value fails inside the `urfave/cli`
framework's `strconv`-based parsing *before* `verify.Run()` ever executes. That error propagates to
`cmd/mpe/main.go`'s `if err := cmd.Run(...); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }`, which always exits 1.

Empirically confirmed against a built binary:

```
$ mpe verify --trusted-now notanumber --bundle b.json --public-key k.pem
Incorrect Usage: invalid value "notanumber" for flag -trusted-now: strconv.ParseInt: ...
exit=1
```

## Impact

MEDIUM. Exit 1 is the "TAMPERED / unverified" outcome. A script gating on `$? -eq 1` to mean
"tampering detected" will false-positive on a mere typo in `--trusted-now`, and the failure is
indistinguishable by exit code from a genuine tamper result. All other flags are `StringFlag`s
validated manually inside `Run()` (correctly producing exit 3), so this is scoped to `--trusted-now`,
but it is the one place the documented contract silently breaks. No test exercises it.

This is **not** a duplicate of `i-3e8a` (open), which concerns `--trusted-now 0` being
indistinguishable from unset; this is about a *non-numeric* value's exit code.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) parse `--trusted-now` as a `StringFlag` and validate/convert inside `Run()` so a bad value
returns the exit-3 path like every other flag, or (b) intercept framework flag-parse errors in
`main.go` and map them to exit 3. Add a test asserting the chosen exit code for a non-numeric value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mpe verify --trusted-now notanumber …` exits with the documented code for an invalid flag
      value (3), not 1.
- [ ] A test covers the non-numeric `--trusted-now` case and asserts the exit code.
- [ ] Docs and behavior agree.

## Files

- `cmd/mpe/main.go` (flag registration / `cmd.Run` error handling, ~244–261)
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/core.go` (`--trusted-now` flag definition; `Usage()` exit-code table)
- `docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md` (exit-code table, ~96)

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-19): verified already implemented in commit bf7183d ("feat(verify): add offline audit bundle verification"). `--trusted-now` is a `cli.StringFlag` (core.go:55-59, not an Int64Flag), validated inside `Run()` via `strconv.ParseInt` and returning exit 3 on failure (core.go:142-150). `verify.md:96` documents exit 3 as covering "invalid flag value". `go test ./pkg/audit/verify/... ./cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/...` passes. Closing as done — the code-review workflow landed this fix but never transitioned the issue.

Reconciliation sweep (2026-07-19): re-audited all remaining open round-4 findings against the current code and confirmed every one was already fixed in commit bf7183d, just never transitioned to closed. Closing i-2kth, i-33dl, i-45eo, i-46g5, i-84pn, i-8pdd, i-4u2g, i-6xaf, i-j03y as done (individual evidence recorded on each issue). With these closed, all 13 fix-priority items in this spec are resolved. `go test ./pkg/audit/verify/... ./cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/...` passes.

title: Unsanitized bundle strings (record_id, root_hash_b64) written to stdout — terminal-escape spoofing
content:
## Problem

Attacker-controlled bundle strings are written to stdout without sanitization:

- `formatRecordLine` (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:69`) interpolates `rec.RecordID`
  (sourced from the bundle via `getString(rm, "record_id")`) straight into `fmt.Sprintf` and out via
  `mustFprintln` — no printability check or escaping.
- The `root=…` hint (`output.go:55–61`) byte-slices `signedRoot["root_hash_b64"]` (`rootHashB64[:n]`,
  `n` capped at 12) for display before it is ever validated as base64, so a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence
  can be cut mid-rune.

Per this tool's own threat model (verify.md: "a bundle … is exactly what an adversary controls"),
these strings are adversary-chosen.

## Impact

LOW/MEDIUM (security, output integrity — not a bypass). A crafted `record_id` containing ANSI /
terminal escape sequences can manipulate an operator's terminal when they run `mpe verify`
interactively — e.g. overwrite or hide prior lines, or spoof a fake `RESULT: OK` line — while the
tool still computes and exits with the genuinely correct (non-zero) code. It cannot spoof the exit
code itself, so scripts checking `$?` are unaffected; the risk is to a human eyeballing terminal
output ("quiet demo, loud reality"). The mid-rune slice can also produce garbled output.

## Suggested fix

Add a single shared "sanitize for display" helper (strip/escape non-printable and control characters,
truncate on rune boundaries) and route all untrusted bundle strings printed to the terminal through
it — `record_id`, the `root_hash_b64` hint, and any similar fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Control/escape characters in `record_id` and other bundle-sourced display strings are stripped
      or escaped before printing.
- [ ] The `root_hash_b64` display hint truncates on rune boundaries (no invalid UTF-8).
- [ ] A test feeds a bundle string containing ANSI escapes and asserts the rendered output is inert.

## Files

- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/output.go:55–69` (`formatRecordLine`, root-hash hint)
- source of `record_id`: `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go` (~493, `getString(rm, "record_id")`)

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-19): verified already implemented in commit bf7183d. `sanitizeForDisplay` (output.go:37-46) and `truncateRunes` (output.go:52-58) are applied to `record_id` (output.go:97) and the `root_hash_b64` hint (output.go:88); the doc-comment at output.go:34 explicitly cites this issue id. Tests in output_test.go cover ANSI/control-char stripping. `go test` passes. Closing as done.

title: rekorAuditPath lacks explicit 0 <= logIndex < treeSize bounds check (inconsistent with merkle.go)
content:
## Problem

`rekorAuditPath` (`pkg/audit/verify/rekor.go:96–128`) walks the RFC 6962 audit path using
parity (`idx /= 2`) without an explicit `0 <= logIndex < treeSize` bounds check first — unlike
`merkle.go`'s `InclusionProof` (explicit range check) and `verify.go`'s `VerifyMerkleInclusion`
(explicit `leafIndex < 0 || leafIndex >= treeSize`). A malformed/buggy
`anchor_refs.rekor.log_index` of `-1` or `>= treeSize` proceeds through the walk instead of being
rejected outright.

## Impact

LOW (hygiene/robustness). Not a forgery vector — the SET signature commits to `logIndex`, and the
final root-hash/checkpoint-pin comparison still gates correctness, so an attacker without the log's
key cannot produce a matching root. But it is inconsistent with this package's explicit-bounds-check
convention and is untested.

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit `0 <= logIndex < treeSize` check at the top of `rekorAuditPath` (or its caller),
returning a clear error, matching the convention in `merkle.go`/`verify.go`. Add a test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rekorAuditPath` rejects `logIndex < 0` or `logIndex >= treeSize` with a returned error.
- [ ] A test covers both out-of-range cases.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor.go:96–128`
- `pkg/audit/verify/rekor_test.go`

feedback.content: Reconciliation (2026-07-19): verified already implemented in commit bf7183d. `rekorAuditPath` now has an explicit `if logIndex < 0 || logIndex >= treeSize` check at rekor.go:97, ahead of the parity walk, consistent with `merkle.go:104` (`InclusionProof`) and `verify.go:137-139` (`VerifyMerkleInclusion`). Closing as done.

title: longToBEBytes documented non-negative invariant not enforced at immudb tx_id/tx_bl_tx_id call sites
content:
## Problem

`longToBEBytes` (`pkg/audit/verify/bytes.go:37–41`) documents "callers only ever pass non-negative …
no overflow to guard against", but `immudb.go`'s `VerifyImmudbALHBinding` / `ComputeImmudbALH` feed
attacker-controlled `tx_id` / `tx_bl_tx_id` (read via `getInt64Loose` straight from the bundle's
immudb anchor block) into it with no explicit non-negative check at the call site.

## Impact

LOW (hygiene). Not a forgery vector — any resulting bit-pattern mismatch simply fails the
ALH-vs-signed-`tx_hash` comparison — but the documented invariant is not actually enforced where it
matters, which is fragile if the helper is reused elsewhere later.

## Suggested fix

Enforce the non-negative precondition at the immudb call sites (reject a negative `tx_id` /
`tx_bl_tx_id` with a clear error), or relax `longToBEBytes`' doc comment to stop asserting an
invariant its callers don't guarantee. Prefer enforcing at the call site.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A negative `tx_id` / `tx_bl_tx_id` from the bundle is rejected with a clear error, or the
      doc-comment no longer claims an unenforced invariant.
- [ ] Behavior and documentation agree.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/bytes.go:37–41`
- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go` (`VerifyImmudbALHBinding`, `ComputeImmudbALH`)

feedback.content:
Fixed: enforced the non-negative precondition at both immudb call sites that feed `longToBEBytes`.

- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go`: `ComputeImmudbALH` now rejects `f.TxID < 0` / `f.BlTxID < 0` with a clear error before computing the inner/ALH hash. `buildImmudbStatePayload` now rejects `txID < 0` before building the ImmutableState signature payload. Both already returned `(..., error)` and their existing callers (`VerifyImmudbALHBinding`, `VerifyImmudbState`) already fail closed on error, so no caller signature changes were needed.
- `pkg/audit/verify/bytes.go`: reworded `longToBEBytes`'s doc comment to stop asserting a blanket "callers only ever pass non-negative" invariant and instead point at the two call sites that now actually enforce it.

    constraints in the spec (independent re-verification of walked candidates, hard-finding on
    genuine absence vs. recovered gap, and a bounded/triggered-only-when-incomplete walk mirroring
    `immudbMaxWindowRoots`).
(b) If the decision is to not implement it, correct the comment at `immudb.go:475-482` to remove
    the false claim.

If (a): add the two regression tests specified in the spec (index-row-only removal recovers
cleanly; index-row + verified-KV removal still produces a finding) using the `fakeAnchorClient`/

feedback.content:
## Decision: (a) Implemented the prev_root_id chain-walk fallback

Chose to implement rather than retract, since `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`'s own `VerifyRootChain` explicitly punts the walk to "the in-service job" (`ChainCaveat`, verify.go:280) — this scan-service code is that job, so retracting would leave no layer actually doing it.

### What changed (`pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go`)

- `EnumerateRootsInWindow` now: SQL-derives candidate root-ids (`rootsInWindow`, unchanged) → fetches/decodes each (`fetchRoots`/`fetchRoot`, factored out of the old inline loop, same "corrupted index row" hard-error as before) → `recoverChainGaps`.
- `recoverChainGaps` triggers a bounded backward walk (via each root's own `prev_root_id`) only on a concrete mismatch, never unconditionally:
  - **Tail gap**: AnchorHead's root-id falls inside the window but isn't the SQL-list's last entry.
  - **Internal gap**: a pairwise check across the SQL-derived list finds `result[i].prev_root_id != result[i-1].RootID`.
  - **Leading gap**: the first (lowest notary_ts_to) entry's own `prev_root_id` is checked once against the window floor.
  - Each walk is bounded by a new `immudbMaxChainWalkSteps` var (shared budget across all walks in one call, same throw-never-silently-truncate convention as `immudbMaxWindowRoots`), and a genuine not-found on a walked-to candidate is a hard error ("does not exist in the anchor's verified store"), never treated as recovered.
  - A recovered root is returned as an ordinary `EnumeratedRoot` — it goes through the exact same signature (step 2a) and anchor-inclusion-proof (step 3) checks scan.go already applies to every root, so it's never trusted purely on the walk's say-so.
- Corrected the false comment (old immudb.go:475-482) that claimed this walk already existed.

### Tests added (`pkg/audit/scan/immudb_chainwalk_test.go`)

Both spec-required regressions pass, plus 3 more covering the tail-trigger path, the legitimate-boundary non-error case, and the walk's own bound:
- `TestImmudbEnumerateRootsInWindowRecoversInternalIndexGap` (spec regression a)
- `TestImmudbEnumerateRootsInWindowGenuineAbsenceIsHardError` (spec regression b)
- `TestImmudbEnumerateRootsInWindowTailGapRecoveredViaAnchorHead`
- `TestImmudbEnumerateRootsInWindowFirstRootBoundaryIsNotAnError`
- `TestImmudbEnumerateRootsInWindowChainWalkBoundedThrows`

`go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes; full repo build/vet clean.

Note on test depth: these exercise `EnumerateRootsInWindow` directly (real `ImmudbClient` over `httptest`, real SQL-index + KV fakes) rather than the full `scan.Scan()` pipeline, because `VerifyAnchorProof`/`AnchorRef` needs real ALH/signature material unrelated to this fix. See separate finding below — that path currently can't validate real data at all, so routing through it wouldn't have let these tests pass regardless of the chain-walk fix's correctness.

### Unrelated finding discovered during this work (not fixed, flagging for a follow-up spec)

While building fixtures I found `ImmudbClient.AnchorRef`'s `entry_hash` (`immudb.go`'s `immudbHTreeLeaf`, `sha256(sha256(key)||sha256(value))` over the raw stored bytes) uses the same formula `pkg/audit/verify`'s `expectedImmudbEntryHash` documents as the disproven predecessor fixed via i-75rl/i-dvp6 (real immudb needs the `0x00`-prefixed/mdLen/kLen HTree leaf construction over the canonical signable-fields JSON, not raw stored bytes). I confirmed by direct probe: `verify.VerifyImmudbEntryHash` returns `false` against `AnchorRef`'s own self-reported `entry_hash` for otherwise-genuine data. This means `VerifyAnchorProof` likely can never return `AnchorVerified` against a real immudb backend today — every root would report a permanent "anchor-proof" finding. No existing test catches this because `scan_test.go` exercises `VerifyAnchorProof` only through `fakeAnchorClient` (which stubs it out entirely); the real-`ImmudbClient` path is explicitly noted as untested (`immudb_test.go`'s comment referencing i-1ahd). Out of scope for s-5910 — recommend filing a dedicated spec.

title: scan: immudb entry_hash uses the formula pkg/audit/verify documents as disproven; step 3 fails on every root
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S1).

## Problem

`pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go:813-818,843`'s `immudbHTreeLeaf`/`AnchorRef` computes `entry_hash` as
`sha256(sha256(key) || sha256(value))` over the raw stored bytes — the exact formula
`pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go:191-193` documents as disproven: *"the earlier `sha256(sha256(root_id) ||
sha256(value))` formula matched no real immudb."* The authoritative construction (byte-verified
against codenotary/immudb 1.11.0) is
`sha256(0x00 || sha256(u16(0) || u16(len(key)) || key || sha256(0x00 || value)))` with
`key = 0x00||root_id`.

`AnchorRef` builds `anchor_refs.immudb` with the retired formula, then `VerifyAnchorProof`
(`immudb.go:887`) hands it to `verify.VerifyImmudbAnchor(..., required=true, ...)`, whose Part 4
recomputes with the *correct* formula and compares — they can never match. Part 1 (folding
`entry_hash` up the audit path to `tx_eH`) fails for the same reason.

## Already independently discovered, never followed up

`i-5j2n`'s closing feedback (2026-09-09) found this exact bug while working on something else,
confirmed by direct probe that `verify.VerifyImmudbEntryHash` returns `false` against `AnchorRef`'s
own self-reported `entry_hash`, and recommended a dedicated follow-up spec. That spec was never
filed — this issue is it.

## Confirmed fixable now, Go-side only

Read the live `mpe-iam-lite` notary source directly (`/Users/ghaskins/sandbox/git/mpe-iam-lite`,
branch `tamper-resistance`, commit `796d7d3`, 2026-09-09):

- `notary/canonical.clj`'s `signable-root-bytes` is exactly
  `canonical-json-bytes(select-keys(payload, signable-root-fields))` — the same 10-field list as Go's
  `SignableRootFields`, byte-for-byte.
- `notary/anchor/immudb.clj`'s `append-root!` writes **exactly this narrowed value** — no more, no
  less — as the immudb KV entry.

This confirms the `s-16qk` notary-side cutover has landed, `verify/immudb.go`'s
`expectedImmudbEntryHash` (signable-subset only) is correct, and `scan/immudb.go`'s formula is
confirmed wrong — not a design ambiguity, a straightforward "didn't get the fix `pkg/audit/verify`
got."

## Failure scenario

Any `mpe verify completeness` run against a real immudb deployment emits an `anchor-proof` finding
for 100% of roots and exits 2. `anchor_refs.immudb` written into counter-example bundles carries the
same wrong `entry_hash`, so those bundles also fail `mpe verify record` Step 7. Fail-closed (not a
forgery path), but the immudb tier's only cryptographic step is non-functional — an operator seeing
it fire on every root will learn to ignore the one check where a real anchor forgery would surface.

## Fix

- Delete `immudbHTreeLeaf`; export and reuse `pkg/audit/verify`'s implementation of the correct HTree
  leaf construction (the "kept independent so this package has no dependency on that package's
  unexported field-struct shape" rationale at `immudb.go:682-685` doesn't hold — `ImmudbALHFields` is
  already exported).
- Add a test driving a canned real-gateway `verifiable/get` response end-to-end through
  `VerifyAnchorProof` (currently zero coverage of the success path — see test-quality note in the
  spec).
- Fix the stale doc at `verify/immudb.go:22-23`, which still states the retired formula and is the
  likely source of the copy-paste.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scan/immudb.go`'s `entry_hash` computation matches `pkg/audit/verify`'s (ideally by calling the
      same shared implementation, not a parallel reimplementation).
- [ ] A test drives a real-shaped immudb `verifiable/get` response through `VerifyAnchorProof` and
      asserts `AnchorVerified`.
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/... ./pkg/audit/verify/...` passes; `go vet`/`golangci-lint`/
      `staticcheck` clean.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go:810-889`
- `pkg/audit/verify/immudb.go:180-237` (ground truth to reuse)
- `pkg/audit/scan/immudb_test.go` (add the success-path test)

title: scan: immudb tier has no source for root_signature_b64; step 2a unconditionally fails (blocked on new mpe-iam-lite endpoint)
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S1b). Tracked separately from [[i-r4v1]] (the entry_hash
formula fix) because this one is blocked on notary-side work; the formula fix should not wait on it.

## Problem

`scan.go:108` calls `verify.VerifyRootSignature(root.Payload, cfg.NotaryPubKey)` for step 2a
(root-signature verification), which requires `root_signature_b64` to be present in `root.Payload`.
For the immudb tier, `root.Payload` comes from decoding the immudb KV entry's stored value
(`fetchRoot` in `immudb.go`) — and per [[i-r4v1]]'s investigation of the live `mpe-iam-lite` source,
that stored value is *by design* narrowed to just the 10 signable fields (no signature at all).

Confirmed by reading `persistence/driver/notary/signed_root_index.clj`'s own docstring in
`mpe-iam-lite` (`tamper-resistance` branch): *"immudb narrows its anchored value to the canonical
signable fields, so it cannot serve the full payload back on a cold read."* The notary's answer for
the offline bundle-assembly path is a separate, non-authoritative Elasticsearch read-model
(`signed_root_index`, populated by the `LeafIndexMaterializer`) that `notary/bundle.clj` consults for
the full signed root.

**This read-model is not exposed to the online completeness scanner at all.** Checked
`subservice/gateway/notary_rest.clj` directly: its only consumer of
`signed-root-index/get-signed-roots` is internal, inside `record-existence-rows`, solely to compute
the `authorized_absent` flag server-side (see [[i-r4v2]]). No REST endpoint serves a full signed root
(with `root_signature_b64`) to the Go scan client for the immudb tier.

## Consequence

`scan.go`'s step 2a is *unconditionally* broken against the immudb tier — independent of and in
addition to [[i-r4v1]]'s entry_hash formula bug. Even after that formula fix lands, every immudb root
would still emit a `root-signature` finding, because there is no signature in the payload to check.

## Fix

Requires new notary-side work (tracked here as blocked, not fakeable from the Go side): expose an
endpoint (e.g. under `/api/v1/notary/*`, matching the existing `leaves`/`record-existence` pattern)
that serves the full signed root (including `root_signature_b64`) from `signed_root_index` to the
online scanner, for roots anchored via the immudb tier. Once that lands:

- Add a client method to `pkg/audit/scan/notary_client.go` for the new endpoint.
- Wire `scanOnePartition`'s step 2a to source the signature-bearing payload from this endpoint (for
  the immudb tier only — S3's stored object already carries the full signed payload, confirmed via
  `notary/anchor/s3.clj`'s `append-root!`, so this doesn't affect that tier).

Per this repo's established convention for a cross-repo blocker (see `s-9vbo`'s `i-H1b`/`s-xhch`
precedent), the actual notary-side endpoint work should be tracked as its own spec/issue in
`mpe-iam-lite`'s own sudocode store, not faked here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Either: a new `mpe-iam-lite` endpoint exists and this repo's scan client consumes it, closing
      the gap — or, if the design changes (e.g. immudb's stored value is widened instead), this issue
      is updated/closed to reflect the actual resolution.
- [ ] `mpe verify completeness` against a real immudb deployment can pass step 2a for a genuinely
      valid root.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:107-113` (step 2a call site)
- `pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go` (`fetchRoot`, `EnumerateRootsInWindow`)
- `pkg/audit/scan/notary_client.go` (would need a new client method)
- `mpe-iam-lite`: `service/src/manetu/iamlite_service/subservice/gateway/notary_rest.clj`,
  `persistence/driver/notary/signed_root_index.clj` (ground truth for what's missing)

## Status

Blocked — pending notary-side endpoint work in `mpe-iam-lite`.

title: scan: authorized_absent trusted verbatim from the notary proxy; TrustedNowMs never read
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S2).

## Problem

`scan.go:254`:
```go
if row.AuthorizedAbsent != nil && *row.AuthorizedAbsent {
    continue // ILM-expected absence, not a tamper signal
}
```

This bool comes straight off the iam-lite `/api/v1/notary/record-existence` response
(`notary_client.go:146-149`). It is the single flag that converts a missing record from a tamper
finding into a pass, and the scan performs zero independent evaluation. `Config.TrustedNowMs` —
documented as the trusted wall-clock that "must not be read from anywhere anchor- or
service-controlled" — is set by the CLI (`completeness/config.go:187`) and never read anywhere in
`pkg/audit/scan` (grep-confirmed). Meanwhile `verify.AuthorizedFloor` is exported and the root's
`retention_policy` is one of the ten *signed* fields already in hand.

## Independently confirmed at the source

Read `mpe-iam-lite`'s `subservice/gateway/notary_rest.clj` directly (`tamper-resistance` branch,
commit `796d7d3`): `record-existence-rows` computes `authorized_absent` via
`(verify/retention-floor-ok? notary-ts-to (:retention_policy root-payload) (System/currentTimeMillis))`
— **the notary service's own wall clock**, not anything cryptographically bound to the response.
Unlike every other field this endpoint returns (genuinely self-authenticating, per this package's own
`doc.go`/`notary_client.go:19-23` claims), `authorized_absent` is a bare, unsigned server assertion by
design. This is not a hypothetical "what if the proxy lies" concern — the scanner's own
recomputation is the *only* possible check on this field; there is nothing to cross-verify it against
on the wire.

## Failure scenario

Deployment runs `retention_policy = {"mode":"retain-all"}` (floor 0 — every record must be present).
Attacker deletes a record and has the proxy answer
`{"id":"...","found":false,"authorized_absent":true}`. Scan `continue`s → zero findings →
`RESULT: OK (exit 0)`, even though the root's own signed policy makes authorized absence logically
impossible.

## Fix

Compute `floor, err := verify.AuthorizedFloor(rp, cfg.TrustedNowMs)` from the root's signed
`retention_policy` (already available as `root.Payload["retention_policy"]`); reject
`authorized_absent == true` whenever `root.notary_ts_to >= floor`; fail closed on `err` (never
silently treat a parse failure as "authorized-absent is fine").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `authorized_absent: true` from the proxy is independently recomputed against the root's signed
      `retention_policy` and `cfg.TrustedNowMs`, not accepted verbatim.
- [ ] A test: `retention_policy: retain-all`, proxy claims `authorized_absent: true` for a record
      inside the floor → scan produces a `record-existence` finding (not a silent pass).
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:200-271` (step 7-8 loop, specifically :254)
- `pkg/audit/verify/retention.go` (`AuthorizedFloor`, already exported and reusable)
- `pkg/audit/scan/scan_test.go`, `pkg/audit/scan/fakes_test.go` (add the regression + teach the fake
  to express the attack)

title: scan: record-existence rows never reconciled against requested ids; an omitted row is a silent pass
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S3).

## Problem

`scan.go:250`'s loop is `for _, row := range rows` — it iterates what the server chose to *return*,
never what was *requested* (`ids`). `NotaryClient.RecordExistence` (`notary_client.go:139-153`)
performs no coverage check either.

This directly falsifies the package's own stated threat model: `doc.go:11-14` and
`notary_client.go:19-23` both claim "a compromised service can only omit rows, which the scan's
density/existence checks already catch." Omission is exactly what is *not* caught by this loop.

## Failure scenario

A batch has 500 leaves. A compromised proxy streams back 499 rows, omitting the one for a deleted
record. No entry for that id in `rows` → the loop never visits it → no finding → exit 0.

Unrepresentable in the current test harness: `fakes_test.go:97` loops the requested ids and always
emits exactly one row per id, so this attack has no way to be expressed in a test today.

## Fix

Build `pending := set(ids)` per chunk (matching the existing `RecordExistenceBatchSize` chunking at
`scan.go:241-246`); delete an id from `pending` on each row received; after the response, emit a
`record-existence` finding for every id still in `pending` (detail: "record existence could not be
confirmed — the notary proxy omitted this id from its response").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fakeNotaryClient`'s `RecordExistence` can be configured to omit a row for a specific id.
- [ ] A test: request 3 ids, fake returns rows for only 2 → scan produces a `record-existence`
      finding for the omitted id.
- [ ] Every id in a chunk is accounted for by either a row or a finding — no id can pass through
      silently.
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:241-270`
- `pkg/audit/scan/notary_client.go:115-153`
- `pkg/audit/scan/fakes_test.go:97` (teach the fake to drop a row)
- `pkg/audit/scan/scan_test.go` (add the regression)

title: scan: found:true is accepted without binding to the anchor-verified leaf hash/signature
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S4).

## Problem

`scan.go:251-252`:
```go
if row.Found {
    continue
}
```
`RecordExistenceRow.LeafHashB64`/`.SignatureB64` (`types.go:115-116`, populated by
`notary_client.go:144-145`) are the exact self-authenticating fields collected for this purpose, and
are grep-confirmed never read by any non-test code. The scan reads only `row.Found`.

## Failure scenario

Attacker deletes a record; a compromised proxy answers
`{"id":"...","found":true,"leaf_hash_b64":"","signature_b64":""}`. Scan `continue`s at :252 — that is
forged evidence accepted at face value, which the package's own threat model (`doc.go:11-14`) claims
is impossible ("a compromised service can only omit evidence, never forge it"). The material to
prevent it is already in hand and anchor-verified: `leaf.LeafHashB64` from `/leaves` was folded into
the Merkle root that step 7 just proved equals the anchor-signed `root_hash_b64` — so a `found:true`
row's own leaf hash can and should be checked against it.

## Fix

Where `row.Found` is true, require `row.LeafHashB64 == leaf.LeafHashB64` (the leaf already fetched via
`/leaves` and used in step 7's Merkle recompute) and verify `row.SignatureB64` over that leaf hash with
`cfg.NotaryPubKey` (mirroring `verify.VerifyRecordIntegrity`'s per-record check in `pkg/audit/verify`).
A mismatch on either is a `record-existence` finding, not a silent pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `found: true` row whose `leaf_hash_b64` doesn't match the corresponding leaf from `/leaves`
      produces a finding.
- [ ] A `found: true` row whose `signature_b64` doesn't verify against `cfg.NotaryPubKey` produces a
      finding.
- [ ] A genuinely correct `found: true` row still passes cleanly (no false positive).
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:250-252`
- `pkg/audit/scan/types.go:100-123` (`LeafRow`, `RecordExistenceRow`)
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go` (`VerifyRecordIntegrity`, the pattern to mirror)
