title: scan: total window wipe defeats step 6's own whole-window-wipe check
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S5).

## Problem

`scan.go:342`:
```go
for p := int64(0); p < maxPartCount; p++ {
```
`maxPartCount` is derived only from `partition_count` on roots that were *actually enumerated*
(`scan.go:103`). If no requested partition returns any root at all, `maxPartCount` stays 0 and this
loop — including the whole-window-wipe branch at `:358-364` written specifically for this case — never
runs a single iteration.

## Failure scenario

The common single-partition deployment: `--partitions 0 --from-ts 1000 --to-ts 2000`. Attacker issues
`DeleteObject` (no version id) on every `roots/0/*.json` in the window — permitted even under Object
Lock COMPLIANCE mode, since it only adds a delete marker, after which `ListObjectsV2` omits them.
Enumeration returns `[]`; steps 4/5 need `len(roots) > 0`; steps 7/8 iterate nothing; step 6 runs zero
iterations because `maxPartCount == 0`. Output: `partition 0: 0 roots, 0 leaves (idle)` /
`RESULT: OK (exit 0)` — every audit record in the window is gone and the scan reports clean.

`TestScanWholePartitionDropIsFinding` only covers the case where a *different, surviving* partition
attests `partition_count`, so this specific single-partition-wiped-entirely case has no test coverage.

## Fix

Iterate `requested ∪ [0, maxPartCount)`, not just `[0, maxPartCount)`, so a requested partition with
zero roots and zero anchor-head still faces the head-inside-window test that step 6 already implements
for the multi-partition case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single requested partition with zero enumerated roots and zero `AnchorHead` response still
      gets evaluated by step 6 (not skipped because `maxPartCount == 0`).
- [ ] A test: one partition requested, anchor returns no roots and no head for it at all → scan
      produces a `partition-coverage` finding (the "whole-partition drop" case, not silently "idle").
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:339-369`
- `pkg/audit/scan/scan_test.go` (add the regression, distinct from
  `TestScanWholePartitionDropIsFinding`)

title: scan: tail check compares only to_seq, never the head's root id; a withheld tail heartbeat is invisible
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S6).

## Problem

`scan.go:184-198`'s doc comment states the intended invariant: *"only when the head's own
notary_ts_to is still within [FromTS, ToTS) must the last enumerated root actually **BE** the head."*
The implementation only checks `case ok && lastToSeq < head.ToSeq` — it never compares root ids.

## Failure scenario

Window ends with batch R4 (`covered_range {80,99}`) followed by heartbeat R5 (`{99,99}`,
`tree_size 0`, `notary_ts_to` inside the window). Head = `{RootID:"R5", ToSeq:99}`. Attacker
delete-markers R5. Last enumerated is R4 with `lastToSeq == 99 == head.ToSeq` — the comparison is
false, so no `tail-truncation` finding fires. Heartbeats always have this property by construction
(step 4's own contiguity rule for a heartbeat is `curFrom == curTo == prevTo`), so the tail heartbeat
of *any* window is freely deletable without detection.

`immudb.go:608-619` gets this exact check right elsewhere in the same package
(`result[len(result)-1].RootID != head.RootID`), making this an inconsistency rather than a deliberate
design choice.

## Fix

When the head is inside the window (`head.NotaryTsTo < cfg.ToTS`), also require
`last.RootID == head.RootID` in addition to the existing `to_seq` comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A withheld tail heartbeat (last enumerated root's `to_seq` equals the head's `to_seq`, but its
      root id differs from the head's) produces a `tail-truncation` finding.
- [ ] The existing non-heartbeat tail-truncation case (`TestScan*Tail*` if present, or equivalent)
      still passes unchanged.
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:174-198`
- `pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go:608-619` (the correct pattern already implemented elsewhere)
- `pkg/audit/scan/scan_test.go` (add the regression)

title: scan: anchor head pointer is unauthenticated; S3's malformed-pointer parse fails open into step 6
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section S7). ## Problem, two parts **(a) No verification of the head pointer itself.** S3's `AnchorHead` (`s3.go:113-133`) is a plain `GetObject` of the *mutable* `roots/

/latest.json` — no WORM check, no checksum, covered by no notary signature. immudb's `AnchorHead` calls `verifiableGet` (which returns the full inclusion proof, tx header, and state signature) and then discards every proof field, reading only `entry.Entry.Value`. So on the tier whose `Tier()` string literally claims `immudb:cryptographic-tamper-evidence`, the head pointer is trusted blindly. An attacker able to write `latest.json` (Object Lock forbids mutating a version, not adding one) can set `to-seq` at or below the surviving tail, or `notary-ts-to` at or above the window end, disabling step 5's tail check outright — and step 6 reads the exact same value. **(b) Discarded ok-flags fail open, specifically into step 6.** `s3.go:126-131`: ```go rootID, _ := getString(m, "root-id") toSeq, _ := getInt64(m, "to-seq") notaryTsTo, _ := getInt64(m, "notary-ts-to") ``` A `latest.json` that exists but lacks the expected keys (schema drift, truncated write, wrong case) yields a **non-nil, all-zero** `AnchorPointer`. The code comment at `:128-130` claims a zero `notary-ts-to` "only ever makes scan step 5's tail check MORE cautious, never less" — true for step 5, but **false for step 6** (added later, reads it in the opposite direction): `ps.head.NotaryTsTo < cfg.FromTS` is `0 < FromTS` → true → `continue` at `scan.go:358-360` → the partition is classified idle and the whole-window-wipe check ([[i-r4v5]]) is skipped. Combined with that issue, a legacy/malformed pointer plus a full-window delete scans clean. ## Fix - Return an error (not a zero-valued pointer) when `root-id`/`to-seq` are absent from a parsed `latest.json` — fail closed on malformed pointer data rather than silently degrading. - Treat `NotaryTsTo == 0` as *unknown*, not "outside the window": when unknown, force the step-6 check to run rather than `continue`-ing as idle. - Verify the immudb head entry using `verify.VerifyImmudbAnchor` with the proof material `verifiableGet` already returns (currently discarded). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A malformed/legacy S3 `latest.json` (missing `root-id` or `to-seq`) surfaces as an error, not a silently-idle partition. - [ ] A `NotaryTsTo == 0` head pointer no longer causes step 6 to skip a partition as idle. - [ ] immudb's `AnchorHead` cryptographically verifies the entry it reads, using proof material already available from `verifiableGet`. - [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes. ## Files - `pkg/audit/scan/s3.go:104-144` - `pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go` (`AnchorHead`) - `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:339-369` (step 6, the consumer of the fixed semantics) - `pkg/audit/scan/s3_test.go`, `pkg/audit/scan/immudb_test.go` (add regressions)

title: verify: set-bundle chain walk needs adjacency-gated per-partition grouping; legitimate bundles report FAILED
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section V1).

## Problem

`verifyMultiRecord` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:649-690`) sorts every root in `signed_roots` into one
global list and requires `roots[i].root_hash_b64 == roots[i+1].prev_root_hash_b64` for every adjacent
pair in that sort order. It never checks that the two roots *claim* adjacency
(`roots[i+1].prev_root_id == roots[i].id`), and never groups by `signed_root.partition`. Neither
assumption holds for a real set bundle:

- Set bundles come from `verify_result_set(record_ids: [...])` with up to 500 **arbitrary** record ids
  (`verification-bundle-schema.md:30-44`). Two records picked at random land in non-adjacent batches.
- Root chains are **per-partition**: the S3 anchor key is `roots/<partition>/<root_id>.json`
  (`verification-bundle-schema.md:484`), and `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:125` gets the adjacency check
  right (`curPrevID != prev.RootID || ...`) — this code doesn't.

## Failure scenario

An auditor runs `verify_result_set(["<id-in-batch-5>", "<id-in-batch-97>"])` against a single
partition. `sortedRoots = [root-5, root-97]`; root-5's `root_hash_b64` is compared against root-97's
`prev_root_hash_b64` (which is actually root-96's hash); they differ → `ChainFailed` → **exit 1,
`Chain continuity: FAIL — gap at seq 900`**. Every record verified, every root signature verified,
nothing tampered — and the tool reports tampering. A two-partition bundle fails identically.

This contradicts the documented contract: `docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md:167-169` defines `FAIL`
as "Predecessor's own signature was invalid, or `prev_root_hash_b64` did not match" and `CAVEAT` as "a
claimed predecessor was **not embedded in this bundle**". A non-adjacent neighbor is exactly the
CAVEAT case. The single-record path (`VerifyRootChain`, `verify.go:272-296`) already gets this right.
It also re-introduces the completeness verdict `verification-bundle-schema.md:400-413` explicitly
retired for set bundles ("a static, offline bundle cannot reliably prove a record was deleted").

## Fix (adjacency-gated, per-partition)

```
group sortedRoots by signed_root.partition
for each adjacent pair (a, b) within a group:
    if b.prev_root_id != a.id:                                   -> ChainCaveat  (predecessor not embedded)
    elif a.root_hash_b64 == "" or a.root_hash_b64 != b.prev_root_hash_b64:  -> ChainFailed  (genuine broken link)
    else:                                                          -> ChainOK
```
Keep the existing `prevHash == ""` fail-closed guard from i-9e8c (don't vacuously match two absent
hashes). Non-adjacent and multi-partition bundles now report `ChainCaveat`, exit 0; a genuine broken
link (same `prev_root_id`, corrupted hash) still reports `ChainFailed`, exit 1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A set bundle with two roots in the same partition but non-adjacent (a gap root absent from
      `signed_roots`) reports `ChainCaveat`, exit 0 — not `ChainFailed`.
- [ ] A set bundle spanning two partitions (each internally consistent) reports `ChainCaveat`, exit 0.
- [ ] The existing genuine-broken-link regression (same `prev_root_id`, corrupted
      `prev_root_hash_b64`) still reports `ChainFailed`, exit 1.
- [ ] The i-9e8c vacuous-match guard (`prevHash == ""` must not match an equally-absent
      `nextPrevHash`) still holds.
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/verify/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:649-690`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go` (existing fixtures at `:108-124,640-701` are all hand-built
  chain-adjacent, single-partition — add the two new cases above)

title: record CLI: ANSI-injection sanitization doesn't cover ChainDetail or AnchorCmds
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section M0).

## Problem

The i-33dl ANSI-injection sanitization fix exists specifically because bundle content is
attacker-controlled and a crafted string carrying ANSI/terminal escapes can rewrite or hide prior
output on an operator's screen (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/output.go:29-36`). It's applied to
`RecordID` and the root-hash hint (`:88,:94`) but not to:

- `result.ChainDetail` (`output.go:141`), sourced from `VerifyRootChain`'s `Detail`
  (`verify.go:279-280`), which embeds bundle-controlled `prev_root_id` verbatim.
- Any `AnchorCmds` value (`output.go:180-190`), built from bundle-controlled
  `bucket`/`key`/`version_id`/`database` in `anchorCommandsFor` (`verify.go:300-325`).

## Failure scenario

A bundle with a non-genesis root whose `prev_signed_root` is not embedded and
`prev_root_id = "\x1b[2K\x1b[1A\rRESULT: OK (exit 0)"`, while the record itself is genuinely tampered.
`VerifyRootChain` returns `ChainCaveat` with that string in `Detail` — independent of whether the
record verified — and it prints raw, capable of visually overwriting the real `TAMPERED`/`FAILED`
lines on an operator's terminal. Exit code is unaffected (scripts are safe); only interactive/human
review is deceived — the exact class of bug i-33dl already fixed once, regressed on two different
fields.

No existing test covers `prev_root_id` or `AnchorCmds` injection — `output_test.go` only
regression-tests `RecordID` and the root-hash hint.

## Fix

Route both `result.ChainDetail` and each `AnchorCmds` value through the existing
`sanitizeForDisplay` at their print call sites.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A bundle with control characters embedded in `prev_root_id` (surfacing via `ChainDetail`)
      prints no raw control bytes.
- [ ] A bundle with control characters embedded in an `anchor_refs.s3.bucket`/`key`/`version_id`/
      `database` field (surfacing via `AnchorCmds`) prints no raw control bytes.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/...` passes.

## Files

- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/output.go:141,180-190`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/output_test.go` (add the two regressions)

title: verify: set-bundle all-skipped anchors print nothing, unlike single-record bundles in the identical case
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section M0b).

## Problem

When every root's anchor check is `Skipped`, `verifyMultiRecord` sets
`Result.ImmudbResult`/`S3Result` to `nil` (`verify.go:706-717,731-742`) — the code comment claims this
is "nothing to summarize, matching the prior single-root-bundle behavior." But `verifySingleRecord`
(`verify.go:431-432,459-460`) *always* populates a non-nil `&immudbR`/`&s3R`, so a single-record
bundle with no anchors prints an explicit `immudb anchor: SKIPPED — no immudb anchor in bundle` line
(`output.go:149,160` guard on `!= nil`), while a set bundle in the identical scenario prints nothing at
all. The parity claim in the comment is false, and the two bundle shapes give inconsistent
observability for equivalent input.

`TestRun_SetBundlePerRecordHintsMatchOwnRoot` hits this exact all-skipped path but asserts nothing
about the (absent) line, so this has no regression coverage today.

## Fix

Make `verifyMultiRecord` populate a `Skipped` result (matching the single-record convention) instead
of `nil` when `verified == 0` in both the immudb and s3 aggregation branches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A set bundle where every root's immudb/s3 anchor is skipped prints an explicit `SKIPPED` line,
      matching single-record behavior for the same scenario.
- [ ] `TestRun_SetBundlePerRecordHintsMatchOwnRoot` (or a new test) asserts the line is present.
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/verify/... ./cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:692-745`
- `pkg/audit/verify/verify_test.go` / `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/core_test.go`

title: verify: set-bundle record_id is a cosmetic label, never bound to the verified content
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section M1).

## Problem

`recordID` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:526-559`) is read from the bundle entry and carried into
`RecordResult.RecordID` purely for display. Nothing ties it to `record_pb_b64`, which is the only
thing the leaf hash and signature actually cover. A bundle producer can relabel which `record_id`
appears next to which genuinely-verified record.

## Failure scenario

An auditor asks "is record `r-42` intact?" The bundle labels record `r-99`'s genuinely-signed payload
as `r-42`. Output reads `Record r-42: VERIFIED`. Both records are authentic; the *identity* the
auditor actually asked about was never checked. The repo now has the `AccessRecord` proto (added in
commit `16ce016`), so decoding `record_pb_b64` and comparing its own id field is feasible.

## Fix

Decode `record_pb_b64` as an `AccessRecord` protobuf and compare its own id field against the bundle's
asserted `record_id`; a mismatch is a `TAMPERED` finding for that record, not a display-only
discrepancy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A set-bundle entry whose `record_id` doesn't match the decoded record's own id inside
      `record_pb_b64` is reported as tampered, not silently displayed under the wrong label.
- [ ] A genuinely matching bundle still verifies cleanly (no false positive).
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/verify/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:517-560` (`verifyMultiRecord`)
- proto package added in `16ce016` (ground truth for the `AccessRecord` shape)

title: scan: S3 leading-edge root deletion is a documented caveat but never surfaced anywhere
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section M2).

## Problem

Both the chain check (`scan.go:115-121`) and the contiguity check (`scan.go:148`) are
`if prev != nil`-guarded, so the first enumerated root's own claimed
`prev_root_id`/`prev_root_hash_b64`/`from_seq` are never checked against anything. The code comment
at `:116-120` explicitly calls this out as intentional ("that boundary is a caveat, not a failure") —
but no caveat is ever recorded in `Finding`, `PartitionSummary`, or `Result`, so an operator sees a
clean `RESULT: OK` with no indication the leading edge of the window was left unverified.

The immudb client closes this hole elsewhere in the same package (`immudb.go:644-652` walks
`prev_root_id` backward via the verified KV store); the S3 client has no equivalent, so the two
anchor tiers give materially different assurance under the identical reported verdict.

## Fix

At minimum, render a per-partition caveat (e.g. `LeadingEdgeUnverified`) analogous to the existing
`HeadOutsideWindow` field, surfaced by `printResult`. Better: give the S3 client a `FetchRoot`
equivalent to validate the first root's claimed predecessor link, mirroring immudb's
`recoverChainGaps`/backward-walk approach.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An operator scanning a window whose first root claims a predecessor outside the window sees an
      explicit signal that the leading edge was not verified (not silent).
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:100-169`
- `pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go:644-652` (the pattern to potentially mirror for S3)
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/completeness/output.go` (if a new caveat field needs rendering)

title: scan: unbounded network reads and no client timeouts on every anchor/notary-proxy path
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section M3). Reported by delegated review; not independently
re-verified line-by-line by the coordinating pass, but plausible and worth a look — flagged as such.

## Problem

- `s3.go:104-111` and `:259`: `io.ReadAll(out.Body)` with no `io.LimitReader`, for `latest.json` and
  every root object.
- `immudb.go:147`/`:167`: same pattern on login/`verifiable/get`/`sqlquery` responses.
- `notary_client.go:63-81`: caps a single NDJSON *line* at 8 MiB but places no bound on row count or
  total response bytes.
- `config.go:39`/`:92`: constructs `&http.Client{}` with no `Timeout`; `NotaryClient.httpClient()`
  falls back to `http.DefaultClient` (also unbounded).

A hostile or wedged endpoint can stream indefinitely (OOM) or hang the scan forever. Contrast
`completeness/config.go:26-35`, which carefully caps the *key file* read at 256 MiB — the discipline
exists in the CLI but not on the network path.

## Fix

`io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(body, maxN))` at every response-body read; a row-count cap in
`readNDJSON`; a sane `Timeout` on both constructed HTTP clients.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `io.ReadAll` on a network response body in `pkg/audit/scan` is preceded by a size cap.
- [ ] Both constructed `http.Client`s have an explicit `Timeout`.
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/audit/scan/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/s3.go:104-111,259`
- `pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go:147,167`
- `pkg/audit/scan/notary_client.go:63-81`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/completeness/config.go:39,92`

title: scan: HeadOutsideWindow never rendered; out-of-scope partitions scanned silently
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (spec section M4). Reported by delegated review; not independently
re-verified line-by-line by the coordinating pass, but plausible and worth a look — flagged as such.

## Problem

`PartitionSummary.HeadOutsideWindow` (`scan.go:335`) is computed and asserted in tests but grep-shows
as never read by `printResult` (`completeness/output.go:50-81`), so "step 5's tail check could not be
evaluated for this window" is invisible to an operator. Separately, `--partitions` is mandatory with
no auto-probe, so a narrower `--partitions` list than the stream's actual `partition_count` silently
scans only part of the log with no signal that other partitions were out of scope.

## Fix

Surface an explicit caveats/scope-note section in `printResult` covering: partitions requested vs.
the widest `partition_count` any enumerated root attested to, and per-partition `HeadOutsideWindow`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `HeadOutsideWindow` is rendered somewhere in `mpe verify completeness` output when true.
- [ ] Scanning with `--partitions` narrower than the stream's attested `partition_count` produces a
      visible note, not silent partial coverage.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/completeness/...` passes.

## Files

- `pkg/audit/scan/scan.go:330-337`
- `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/completeness/output.go:50-81`

title: verify+scan: grab-bag of small determinism/consistency/robustness findings
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (Low/test-quality section — bundled per explicit user direction: each item
is small enough on its own that a dedicated issue per item isn't worth the overhead). Split any of
these out into its own issue on request if one turns out to need more room than expected.

## Items (each independently fixable; tackle in any order)

1. **Nondeterministic anchor-cmd hint on set bundles** — `verify.go:581-588`'s `anchorCmds` ranges a
   Go map and overwrites by key, so the printed cross-check command is an arbitrary one of N roots,
   differing run to run on identical bundle bytes. Inconsistent with the surrounding code's explicit
   determinism discipline (`sortedRoots`, a 50-iteration determinism test at `verify_test.go:695`).
   Fix: iterate root ids in sorted order, or key the printed commands by root id so all N print.

2. **Inverted `state_db`/`database` fallback order** — `verify.go:302-306` prefers `state_db` then
   falls back to `database`; `immudb.go:310-313` does the reverse. On a bundle carrying both with
   different values, the printed hint can name a different DB than the one whose signature was
   actually verified. Fix: make both prefer `state_db`.

3. **`key_id` parsed but never compared** — `verify.go:59-93`/`keys.go:50-60` correctly ignore the
   bundle's `sig_alg` (deriving the algorithm from the key type is the right, algorithm-confusion-proof
   choice — keep that). But `key_id` is unused too, so a wrong notary key reports
   `TAMPERED (signature verification failed)` instead of a clear "wrong key" diagnostic. Fix: add a
   diagnostic-only comparison that never gates the verdict.

4. **`DecodeBundle` ignores trailing JSON** — `jsonutil.go:20-28` never checks `dec.More()`, so
   `{...bundle...}{...second doc...}` verifies the first document and silently discards the rest. Fix:
   check `dec.More()` and reject trailing data.

5. **Self-referential Merkle known-vector tests** — `merkle_test.go:149-196` computes expected hashes
   with the package's own `nodeHash`/`leafNodeHash`, so a swapped/omitted domain-separator byte would
   move both sides of every assertion together. Fix: add one hard-coded digest from a published RFC
   6962 test vector.

6. **Nil-client panic reachable from an errgroup goroutine** — `scan.go:293`: a nil `cfg.Notary`/
   `cfg.Anchor` panics inside a goroutine, crashing the process; `Scan` only validates
   `len(cfg.Partitions)`. Fix: validate both are non-nil up front.

7. **Unsanitized error-body strings in CLI-printed errors** — `immudb.go:263,359` interpolate raw
   `string(resp.body)` into errors the CLI prints, while `output.go:35-44` sanitizes anchor-sourced
   display strings for terminal safety but not error text. Fix: apply the same sanitization.

8. **No chain-walk cycle detection** — `immudbMaxChainWalkSteps = 1_000_000` (`immudb.go:577`) bounds
   a malicious/cyclic `prev_root_id` chain but still performs up to a million sequential
   `verifiable/get` round trips before erroring; each root also costs two round trips (`fetchRoot`,
   then `AnchorRef`) with no caching. Fix: add a visited-set for early cycle termination; consider
   caching the fetched entry between the two call sites.

9. **Not-found classification by substring** — `s3.go:143`, `immudb.go:199-207` classify "not found"
   partly via `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "404")`, which can match unrelated transport errors
   (e.g. `dial tcp ...:404`), converting infrastructure failures into tamper findings or vice versa.
   Fix: prefer typed error checks where the SDK provides them; narrow the substring match.

10. **`--immudb-port` zero-value check** — `completeness/config.go:226-229` uses
    `port := cmd.Int(...); if port == 0 { error }` rather than `cmd.IsSet`, the same anti-pattern
    already fixed elsewhere in this codebase for `--trusted-now`. Low severity (port 0 is never a
    real target) but `--concurrency`/`--record-existence-batch-size` remain framework-parsed
    `IntFlag`s that may share the short-circuit-to-exit-1 issue `record`'s own flags were
    deliberately converted away from — **not confirmed by execution**; run
    `mpe verify completeness --concurrency abc ...` and check the actual exit code before deciding
    whether these need the same `StringFlag` treatment `record` got.

## Additional items reported by delegated review, not independently re-verified — triage before acting

- Enumerated roots' *signed* `partition`/`notary_ts_to` are never cross-checked against the
  partition/window they were enumerated under (membership decided by unsigned S3 key metadata or the
  explicitly-untrusted immudb SQL discovery index).
- `notary_ts_to` ties in enumeration order fall back to `root_id` lexical order, uncorrelated with
  chain order — claimed to produce false `chain`/`contiguity` findings on S3 and an infra-error exit
  on immudb.
- `s3.go:206-210` uses two different key parsers (`rootKeyToNotaryTS` vs `rootKeyToID`) and silently
  `continue`s on disagreement, arguably violating `types.go:78-81`'s "MUST NOT silently truncate"
  contract.
- `s3.go:245-302`'s WORM binding check never verifies the fetched object's bytes actually decode to
  the payload being verified (only compares `sha256(body)` to the server-echoed checksum); and the
  `retain-all` branch only accepts a legal hold, not COMPLIANCE mode with a future retain-until.
- `s3.go:199-202`: `ListObjectsV2`'s `IsTruncated == true` with a nil `NextContinuationToken` re-lists

title: test: Clojure cross-implementation parity fixtures no longer test parity (stale schema 1.0 vs supported 2.0)
content:
Implements [[s-4x0h]] (test-quality section).

## Problem

`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/testdata/parity/{verified,tampered,unsealed}/bundle.json` are all
pinned at `"schema_version": "1.0"`, while `supportedSchemaMajor = "2"`
(`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go:38`). So all three now fail **identically** at the meta-envelope gate —
`parity_test.go:106-107` asserts `exit code == 3` and `stderr contains "unsupported schema_version"`
for every one of the three cases — before any record, signature, Merkle, or chain logic ever runs.

The suite no longer distinguishes verified from tampered from unsealed at all; it only checks that
both implementations reject a stale schema version identically, a much weaker property than the
fixture names and the commit message ("with Clojure-parity test fixtures for the record path") imply.
`TestParityFixturesExist` just counts files (`>= 3`) and doesn't compensate.

The test's own doc comment (`parity_test.go:15-59`) discloses this honestly, and regenerating
schema-2.0 goldens requires the real Clojure CLI plus a private signing key (a separate piece of
infrastructure this repo doesn't have).

## Fix

Either: regenerate the three fixtures at schema 2.0 against the real Clojure reference verifier (once
that infrastructure is available), restoring genuine parity coverage across verified/tampered/unsealed
— or, if that's not feasible right now, add an explicit `t.Skip` with a tracking reference so the
suite stops silently implying a property it no longer tests, rather than three cases whose only
observable difference is a schema-version string that isn't actually exercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Either genuine schema-2.0 parity fixtures exist and exercise record/signature/Merkle/chain
      logic distinctly for verified/tampered/unsealed, or the test suite explicitly skips with a
      clear reason and tracking reference rather than silently passing a weaker check.
